## The five forks

**A. Fate of `VueMacroSemanticInput` and `verter_macro_dto`'s `MacroRuntimeBundle`/`MacroTscBundle`.**
Deleted outright, or retained as an internal emit-stage shape? Guessing wrong either breaks C3's
already-locked vocabulary or leaves a compatibility shim alive — and this codebase deletes superseded
paths rather than keeping both.

**B. Is B6 a real, missing predecessor of C2?** `contracts/compile-transaction.md:8-9`'s stage 1 appears
to need `PreparedCarrier`, which B6 owns, yet the DAG does not list B6 as a C2 predecessor. Either the
DAG has a missing edge or the contract does not really need it. **This one changes a DAG edge if you rule
it real — say so explicitly.**

**C. Which crate owns the concrete project-aware `CompileTypeInfo` lifecycle variant?** This depends on
C1's extraction, which has now been RULED: C1 extracts the module-resolver / non-flow TypeInfo kernel into
the EXISTING `verter_semantic` crate, with a capability-limited observation interface and a closed
inherent gateway (`TypeInfoCore::attempt`). Read
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-C1-FOUR-FORKS.md and

**D. How many first-party lifecycle modes does `CompileTypeInfo` have — three or five?** ADR-003 and the
charter disagree. Resolve from the ratified source.

**E. Do the new anti-replay tokens need the private-`sealed`/single-construction-point pattern?** Note
what the C1 addendum established: Rust has no friend-crate exception, so a private-supertrait seal and a
foreign implementor are mutually exclusive — a sealing design that requires an out-of-crate implementor is
impossible. Rule on the token pattern with that constraint in view.

## Rules for your answer

- Landed enforcement is structural (visibility/E0603, type-state, sealed traits, closed enums matched
  exhaustively) — NEVER a name-keyed source scanner. Do not propose one.
- Effort, breadth and breakage are not reasons to weaken a design.
- Where the charter is factually wrong about the code, say so with the file:line that disproves it.
- For EACH fork, state explicitly whether your ruling changes an accepted ADR, a DAG edge, or a program
  outcome. Fork B in particular may change a DAG edge; the maintainer needs that called out, since it
  determines whether a formal amendment is required.
- Concise, file:line throughout. End with five verdict lines.

    78	## Intent Contract
    79	
    80	**Actor/problem.** Every project-aware compile request (any Vue SFC whose macros or template bindings need
    81	resolved cross-file type information — `defineProps<T>()`, `defineEmits<T>()`, imported `.vue` component
    82	surfaces) is, today, satisfied by a single undifferentiated blocking call
    83	(`VerterHost::compile_with_audit_options` → `vue_macro_compile_input`/`vue_macro_semantic_input` →
    84	`produce_vue_macro_codegen` → `compile_registered_vue_artifact`) with no plan, no anti-replay token, no
    85	partial/resumable outcome, and no proof that the semantic facts consumed at emission are the same facts a
    86	plan actually demanded. `ADR-003`'s rejected alternatives — "public semantic trait object", "compiler
    87	receives host/Engine/provider state", "framework/compiler-local resolver fallback" — are not live risks in
    88	the CURRENT code (there is exactly one bridge type, `VueMacroSemanticInput`, and it already carries no host
    89	reference), but nothing today would catch a **second** one being added, because there is no sealed facade
    90	enforcing it — the current path is safe by absence of temptation, not by structural closure.
    91	
    92	**Required observable outcomes.**
    93	- Every project-aware Vue compile reachable from `VerterHost::compile_with_audit_options` (and any other
    94	  production entry that currently calls `vue_macro_compile_input`/`vue_macro_semantic_input`) runs through
    95	  `prepare -> plan -> project -> emit` exactly as `contracts/compile-transaction.md:5-16` specifies; `plan()`
    96	  discovers the complete semantic-projection demand batch before `project()` runs, and `emit()` discovers no
    97	  new demand (`compile-transaction.md:18`).
    98	- `project()` returns exactly one of `CompleteFacts | NeedInputs(LoadSet) | TerminalFailure`
    99	  (`compile-transaction.md:12-13`) by driving one or more attempts against C1's `AttemptOutcome`
   100	  (`contracts/input-loading.md:11-17`) — a `NeedInputs` outcome from the underlying kernel is a **first-class
   101	  return**, never silently retried-to-blocking inside `project()` itself (that retry/replan loop is the
   102	  caller's job, per `input-loading.md §4` and `compile-transaction.md §4`).
   103	- `emit()` validates the whole `CompilePlanToken`, then validates the facts against the exact
   104	  `ProjectionPlanToken` the containing plan referenced, before constructing any output
   105	  (`compile-transaction.md:53`) — missing, extra, duplicated, reordered-without-canonical-identity, stale,
   106	  wrong-profile, wrong-projection-plan, wrong-root, or wrong-domain facts are rejected before
   107	  `compile_registered_vue_artifact`'s codegen body (or its replacement) ever runs.
   108	- `CompileTypeInfo<'_>` is a concrete, Verter-owned, sealed type; every one of its lifecycle-variant
   109	  constructors is a first-party construction (ADR-003:11) reachable only from inside its owning crate(s).
   110	- Zero-demand compiles (no macro needs project data) construct no `CompileTypeInfo` session, run no module
   111	  resolver or TypeInfo work, and represent the projection stage as an empty complete batch bound to the plan
   112	  (`compile-transaction.md:57-61`) — this is the steady-state path for the large majority of Vue SFCs (any
   113	  file whose macros are all runtime-object-literal or unresolved-type-free) and must not regress in cost
   114	  versus today's `Unavailable`-fast-path.
   115	- The four duplicate/near-duplicate resolve call sites named in Context (three in
   116	  `host_compile_audit.rs:499-507,578-586,612-620` plus the private/public duplicate at `:670-681` vs.
   117	  `vue_macro_codegen.rs:649-660`) collapse onto the single new transaction-driving path.
   118	
   119	**Forbidden observable outcomes.**
   120	- A second concrete type or trait that a production call site can pass to `compile_registered_vue_artifact`
   121	  (or its replacement) in place of `CompileTypeInfo` — "compiler-local resolver fallback" (ADR-003's
   122	  rejected alternative) applied to this new facade, not just to the old bridge.
   123	- `CompileTypeInfo` (or any lifecycle variant of it) naming, holding, or being constructible from
   124	  `VerterHost`, the scheduler, or any session-tier type — ADR-003: "compiler receives host/Engine/provider
   125	  state" is rejected; ADR-015: "provider lifecycle never enters direct compiler or semantic kernel"
   126	  (`decisions/ADR-015-binding-dependency-direction.md:30`).
   127	- A blanket `unsafe impl<T> Send for CompileTypeInfo<T>` / `Sync` impl. Ownership/concurrency is a
   128	  **per-lifecycle-variant** property (ADR-003:13) — a borrowed direct-local variant may be legitimately
   129	  `!Send`; an owned validated-precomputed variant may be `Send + Sync`; no single impl may paper over that.
   130	- `emit()` (or anything reachable from it) discovering a new semantic demand, calling into
   131	  `ProjectSemanticDispatch`/the module resolver/TypeInfo directly, or otherwise reopening resolution after
   132	  `project()` returned `CompleteFacts` — that is exactly the "second engine" program.md's exit line forbids.
   133	- Any `project()` implementation that blocks a calling thread to completion internally when driven from an
   134	  I/O-free environment — the entire point of consuming C1's `AttemptOutcome` is that `project()` can return
   135	  `NeedInputs` instead; a `CompileTypeInfo` variant that internally calls a blocking `ResolverContext`
   136	  method and swallows the distinction is not "first-party lifecycle modes", it is the status quo relabeled.
   137	- Stale or replayed `CompileFactsBatch` data reaching codegen — the anti-replay tokens exist specifically so
   138	  that facts computed against plan A can never be accepted by a call validating against plan B, even when
   139	  both plans target the same file.

   141	**Authority/fallback order.** `SemanticQueryKey -> ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute -> SemanticGraphStore`
   142	remains the sole query-time resolver, unchanged by C2 (C1 converges its home crate; C2 never re-implements
   143	or wraps it a second time). `CompileTypeInfo` lifecycle variants are the **only** caller-facing entry a
   144	project-aware compile may use to reach that resolver — never a direct call from `verter_compiler` codegen
   145	into anything C1-owned, and never a second producer function shaped like today's
   146	`produce_vue_macro_codegen`. A `project()` attempt that cannot prove a current, coherent view fails closed
   147	to `TerminalFailure` (mirroring `StoreViewRead`'s current/cold-seed split C1 preserves,
   148	`.claude/skills/host-session/SKILL.md:678-696`) — C2 must not weaken that fail-closed order while adding the
   149	resumable `NeedInputs` outcome alongside it.

   194	## Staged transaction and anti-replay contract
   195	
   196	C2 implements `contracts/compile-transaction.md` verbatim, not a paraphrase of it:
   197	
   198	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized request to the prepared root and everything listed at
   199	  `compile-transaction.md:30-40` (prepared root/source/unit identities, parse key/domain/generation,
   200	  normalized product-request collection, semantic profile when observed, per-product output/terminal
   201	  profiles, framework/compiler compatibility identity, projection schema/domain, plan algorithm
   202	  compatibility domain, deterministic demand ordering and digest).
   203	- The plan additionally owns narrower deterministic tokens — `ProjectionPlanToken` (root + semantic profile
   204	  + closed demand batch + kernel/projection domains), `ProductSubplanToken` (root + framework/product +
   205	  output profile + required product mapping contract), `TerminalSubplanToken` (exact typed result/product +
   206	  requested presentation/provenance/encoding profile) — so a presentation-only change can mint a new
   207	  terminal subplan without invalidating an unchanged semantic-projection or codegen subplan
   208	  (`compile-transaction.md:42`). C2 must not collapse these into one token "for simplicity" — that would
   209	  break the terminal-subplan reuse required by `contracts/compile-transaction.md §7`'s test list
   210	  ("presentation/serialization-only changes reuse unchanged semantic and code subplans").
   211	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds the exact `ProjectionPlanToken` and demand digest, semantic profile and kernel
   212	  compatibility domain, input basis and observed dependency fingerprints, one typed result per demand,
   213	  exactness/completeness/degradation, and integrity/size limits (`compile-transaction.md:44-51`). C2 defines
   214	  this envelope generically; **it does not define the demand/result vocabulary riding inside it** — that is
   215	  C3's locked `MacroPayload`/`DemandResult` (`C3.md:22-56`). C2's obligation is that the envelope's identity
   216	  fields (token, digest, basis, fingerprints) are validated independently of whatever payload type occupies
   217	  the per-demand result slot.
   218	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` from `project()` is resumable, never mutates the current plan/prepared value with
   219	  unversioned data, and the outer orchestrator (the caller of `project()` — today `host_compile_audit.rs`'s
   220	  transaction driver) loads/publishes/rebuilds a coherent input view per `input-loading.md`, then reruns
   221	  `project()` with the same plan only while the plan's basis remains valid; otherwise it replans
   222	  (`compile-transaction.md:64-67`).
   223	- Emission validates the whole `CompilePlanToken` first, then the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`
   224	  (`compile-transaction.md:53`) — two independent checks, not one combined comparison, because a
   225	  presentation-only replan can hold a fresh `CompilePlanToken` while legitimately reusing an unchanged
   226	  `ProjectionPlanToken`'s facts.
   227

   263	## Structural confinement
   264	
   265	- **Sealed-trait / private-constructor closure for `CompileTypeInfo`.** Following the pattern C1 relocates
   266	  for `ResolverContext` (`sealed::Sealed`, a non-`pub` module — `C1.md:329-335`), `CompileTypeInfo`'s
   267	  lifecycle variants are constructible only from inside their owning crate: an external crate cannot
   268	  implement a new lifecycle because the sealing supertrait is not `pub`. This is genuinely structural
   269	  (E0603 privacy) for **external** bypass. It is **not** structural against an internal contributor adding a
   270	  sixth lifecycle variant or a new bypass constructor inside the same crate — that stays review discipline,
   271	  same caveat C1 records for its own sealed trait.
   272	- **Crate-dependency-firewall proof, reused rather than re-invented.** `CompileTypeInfo` must be defined
   273	  inside `verter_compiler` (or a crate `verter_compiler` already depends on, i.e. `verter_semantic` once C1
   274	  relocates the kernel there) — never `verter_session`. `crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:52-62` today has
   275	  no `verter_session`/`verter_workspace`/`verter_scheduler`/`verter_tsgo_api` edge; the existing, landed
   276	  `workspace_dependency_layers.rs` closure guard (the same one `C1.md:320-328` cites) already proves no
   277	  lifecycle variant defined inside `verter_compiler` can name `VerterHost` or the scheduler — because those
   278	  types are structurally unnameable from inside that crate's dependency closure, not because a marker says
   279	  so. This requires no new guard.
   280	- **Anti-replay tokens: privacy blocks external forgery, digest-equality raises the bar on internal
   281	  shortcuts, neither makes internal misuse impossible.** `CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken`/
   282	  `ProductSubplanToken`/`TerminalSubplanToken` should follow `CompileTarget`'s existing "one sealed
   283	  construction point" discipline (`compile/types.rs:17-23`'s own doc comment: "the only production
   284	  construction points are internal... every production entry point takes `CompileRequest` exclusively and
   285	  cannot construct a `CompileTarget` value at all"). Be honest about what this proves: a private constructor
   286	  stops an *external* crate from fabricating a token (E0603). It does **not** stop a contributor *inside*
   287	  `verter_compiler` from adding a second, ad-hoc `pub(crate)` constructor that skips `plan()` — that
   288	  contributor would still need to independently compute a digest that matches what `emit()`'s validation
   289	  expects (`compile-transaction.md:40`'s "deterministic demand ordering and digest"), which raises the cost
   290	  of a silent bypass but is not a compiler-enforced impossibility. This charter does not claim more than
   291	  that; it is recorded here per the explicit instruction to not overclaim "structural" for a convention.
   292	- **Exhaustive closed-enum matching for `AttemptOutcome`/`project()`'s return/`DemandResult`.** A Rust
   293	  `match` with no `_` arm over `CompleteFacts | NeedInputs(LoadSet) | TerminalFailure` (and, one layer down,
   294	  C1's `Complete | NeedInputs | Terminal` and C3's `Success | NotFound | Stale | Error`) is genuinely
   295	  structural: adding a new variant breaks every non-wildcard match at compile time, forcing every call site
   296	  to handle it. The caveat C1 already records for its own `AttemptOutcome` coverage claim (C1-AC-5's "test
   297	  double" argument) applies identically here: this protection is only real as long as no call site uses a
   298	  `_` catch-all arm anywhere in the match. That absence is review-enforced (grepped at review time), not a
   299	  landed scanner, per `CLAUDE.md`'s forward-only landed-scanner rule.
   300	- **`Send`/`Sync` absence is a real auto-trait property, not a marker.** Rust derives `Send`/`Sync`
   301	  automatically from a struct's fields; "no blanket impl" is enforced simply by not hand-writing one and
   302	  letting each lifecycle variant's own field types (a borrowed `&'a` reference vs. an owned `Arc`) determine
   303	  its auto-trait eligibility independently. A reviewer adding a hand-written blanket `unsafe impl` is a
   304	  visible diff at the type definition, not a runtime behavior to detect.
   305	- **What is explicitly NOT claimed as structural here:** "first-party lifecycle modes" as a *count* (how
   306	  many variants `CompileTypeInfo` has) is not fixed by any structural mechanism — nothing stops a
   307	  contributor from adding a sixth lifecycle variant next year with a trivial constructor that compiles fine
   308	  and technically "implements" the sealed trait's required methods with degenerate bodies (return
   309	  `TerminalFailure` unconditionally), exactly the "exhaustive test-double... returns a bare value of the
   310	  right type" failure mode this task's instructions warn against. C2's mitigation is C2-AC-8's test plus
   311	  ordinary review, not a compiler proof; this charter records that honestly rather than asserting a
   312	  guarantee it cannot back.

   314	## Boundary against C1, B5, B6, and C3
   315	
   316	**C1 boundary.** C2 does not define `AttemptOutcome`/`LoadSet`, does not converge `ModuleResolverCore`/
   317	`TypeInfoCore`, and does not touch the crate-relocation C1 performs. C2's `project()` stage is the **first
   318	real consumer** of C1's outcome — it drives repeated attempts, owns the snapshot-extend/retry loop, and owns
   319	the anti-replay tokens, exactly the split C1's own charter states (`C1.md:231-238,365-375`). If C1's actual
   320	landed `AttemptOutcome` shape differs from what this charter assumes (a bare three-arm enum consumable
   321	without further wrapping), C2 must be revised, not silently adapted around a shape C1 never ratified.
   322	
   323	**B5/B6 boundary and gap.** C2 does not own the borrowed one-shot direct compiler core (B5) or the
   324	prepared/direct-batch lifecycle (B6). C2's `emit()` stage is expected to reuse B5's accepted borrowed-core
   325	codegen algorithms. `contracts/compile-transaction.md`'s stage 1 (`prepare(source, parse options) ->
   326	PreparedCarrier`) names the exact deliverable B6's charter describes ("explicit borrowed/owned
   327	preparation... the direct core is final enough for semantic projection... to depend on", `B6.md:5,11`) — yet
   328	`program-dag.toml:169` does not list `B6` as a C2 predecessor. C2 cannot resolve this gap unilaterally; see
   329	Open question §B.
   330	
   331	**C3 boundary.** C2 does not define macro role/demand semantics. C3's charter is already locked
   332	(`C3.md:3`, `PROPOSED amendment / LOCKED`) and names the exact demand vocabulary (`MacroPayload { role,
   333	subject, lane }`) and result envelope (`DemandResult<T> = Success | NotFound | Stale | Error`) that must
   334	ride inside C2's generic `CompileFactsBatch`. C2 must design `CompileFactsBatch`'s per-demand result slot to
   335	be exactly shaped to carry C3's already-fixed types — C2 does not get to renegotiate C3's vocabulary, only
   336	to prove its own envelope can carry it. This is a real coupling constraint this charter cannot discharge
   337	without either an accepted C1 (whose `AttemptOutcome` C3's projection also assumes reachable underneath) or
   338	a reconciliation pass against `C3.md`'s exact field list once implementation starts.

   340	## Required exit
   341	
   342	Per `program.md:205`: **project-aware compilation cannot accept another semantic engine or stale/mismatched
   343	facts.** Concretely: `CompileTypeInfo` is sealed and crate-firewalled so no second engine is nameable from
   344	inside `verter_compiler`; `CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` validation at `emit()` rejects every
   345	stale/wrong-root/wrong-profile/wrong-projection-plan/extra/missing/duplicated fact case before output
   346	construction; the four duplicate/near-duplicate resolve-and-compile call sites in `verter_session` collapse
   347	onto the one transaction driver; the blocking-until-complete `produce_vue_macro_codegen` pattern is retired
   348	as the production path in favor of attempt-shaped calls returning `AttemptOutcome`; zero-demand compiles
   349	remain as cheap as today's `Unavailable` fast path; no `TypeExpr`-general transit, flow semantics, or
   350	C1/C3-owned semantics were introduced inside C2's own deliverable.

   382	**A. Does `VueMacroSemanticInput` (and `verter_macro_dto`'s `MacroRuntimeBundle`/`MacroTscBundle`) get
   383	deleted outright, or survive as an internal emit-stage shape?** `CompileFactsBatch` (C2's, generic) and

     5	
     6	# Verter Architecture Reference
     7	
     8	For domain-specific detail, see: `/type-resolution`, `/type-cache-architecture`, `/component-meta`, `/compiler-codegen`, `/host-session`.
     9	
    10	## Shared Substrate Principle
    11	
    12	Verter is one shared optimized codebase. Consumers reuse lower-level crates instead of separate semantic pipelines.
    13	
    14	- Put reusable parsing, analysis, type-resolution, caching, and import-following behavior in the shared owner crate.
    15	- `verter_language` is the zero-dependency leaf routing authority: `FileLanguage`, `FrameworkAdapterId`, `LanguageId`, `CapabilityId`, and the pure static `LanguageRegistry` (`classify_static(path)` — never reads project config). Host-gated classification (static registry × `ProjectCapabilitySnapshot`) is owned by `verter_session::framework::HostLanguageClassifier`; scheduler/workspace consumers reach it only through session-implemented trait objects (`SourceLoader::classify` / `WorkspaceAccess::classify_file`). The crate is a `verter_span`-only leaf (its design allowance — spans for the parse-artifact regions; strings stay crate-interned) and keeps a crate-local id-intern table: no lower crate exposes a reusable interning facility, and the id set is bounded by registered languages. It also owns the framework-neutral parse payload: `FrameworkParseArtifact` (typed `FrameworkParseCommon` — `ScriptRegion { span, source_type, kind }` / template / style regions, external links, `LanguageDiagnostic`s — plus a PRIVATE erased `Arc<dyn CarrierParse>`), with the raw downcast confined to each adapter's own bridge module (no capability token — a foreign artifact's erased payload is a DIFFERENT concrete `CarrierParse` type, so the `Any` downcast already fails structurally for it); the session's blessed accessors are `FrameworkAdapterCtx::carrier_for::<T>` (routed through each adapter's registered-projector opener, e.g. `open_vue_carrier`) and the Vue adapter's `vue_parse()`; the concrete `VueParseCarrier` + Vue producer live in `verter_compiler::framework_common::vue_bridge`.
    16	- `verter_session` is the shared host/session/cache boundary for host-backed consumers.
    17	- `verter_semantic` and `verter_compiler` own reusable semantics, lowering, and codegen.
    18	- `verter_session::resolver_core` owns the host-backed resolver stack and type-resolution orchestration. Resolver-path methods receive `ctx: &dyn ResolverContext` (sealed super-trait at `resolver_core/resolver_context.rs`) — only `VerterHost` implements it, enforced by the `no_concrete_verter_host_in_seal_scope` arch-guard.
    19	- `verter_protocol` owns transport-facing schema DTOs; `verter_ffi` stays a thin native/WASM adapter layer.
    20	- Consumer packages and apps stay adapter-oriented: thin wrappers, public API shaping, transport glue, UX-specific behavior.
    21	
    22	Bug or slowdown in one surface → fix in shared substrate so other consumers benefit.

    32	| **`@verter/unplugin`** | Universal bundler plugin (Vite, Rollup, webpack, esbuild, rspack, Rolldown, Farm). Compiles `.vue` files via `@verter/native`. Supports `preCompile` for build-start cache warming | `src/index.ts` |
    33	
    34	## Unplugin Configuration (`packages/unplugin/`)
    35	
    36	`@verter/unplugin` provides a `VerterPluginOptions` interface:
    37	
    38	| Option | Type | Default | Description |
    39	| ------ | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
    40	| `componentId` | `(filename, source, isProd) => string` | hash-based | Custom component ID generator |
    41	| `include` | `string \| RegExp \| (string \| RegExp)[]` | `[/\.vue$/]` | File patterns to include |
    42	| `preCompile` | `boolean` | `false` | Pre-compile all `.vue` files during `buildStart`. Scans project root, upserts files into host cache (including type dependencies for macros), and compiles them. When `transform()` later receives same content, host returns cached result instantly. `node_modules` excluded from scanning. |
    43	| `crossFileOptimize` | `boolean` | `false` | Cross-file prop constness optimization. Requires `preCompile: true`. After pre-compilation, analyzes render tree to determine which props are always passed constant values, skipping dynamic tracking in compiled output. |
    44	| `template` | `object` | — | Template compiler options (compat with `@vitejs/plugin-vue`) |
    45	
    46	**`preCompile` architecture:** During `buildStart()`, scans project root for `.vue` files (excluding `node_modules` and dot-directories). For each file: upserts into host, resolves external `src` attributes and macro type dependencies (e.g., `import type { Props } from './types'` used in `defineProps<Props>()`), then triggers compilation. When another plugin modifies the file before `transform()`, host detects content change via internal hashing and recompiles. Third-party `.vue` files in `node_modules` compile on-demand during `transform()` — no pre-compilation overhead.
    47	
    48	**Macro type resolution invariant:** cross-file macro type resolution must only follow imports reachable from the requested type's local declaration graph. Unrelated imports in the same file are out of scope; plain imports are not implicit re-exports.
    49	
    50	## CSS Analysis & Selector Matching (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/`)
    51	
    52	`verter_css_syntax` is the shared lossless token/event authority for CSS, SCSS, indented Sass, Less, and Stylus. `StyleSyntaxIrSink` and `LosslessCstSink` are peers over the same parser event stream. Semantic style analysis projects only complete, static selector nodes into selectors, classes, IDs, custom properties, and at-rules; interpolation, recovery, and evaluation-dependent selectors fail closed. Each `AnalyzedCssClass` carries `selector_index` (exact class → comma-part selector join) and each `AnalyzedSelector` carries `rule_body_span` (brace- or indentation-delimited body span). Vue's planner separately consumes trusted IR for authored-dialect `v-bind()` and post-preprocess plain-CSS module hashing/scoping; Svelte consumes the IR as a trust gate for its distinct plain-CSS matcher/scoper. Svelte's carrier/CSS parser remains the compatibility owner until exact Svelte 5.56.3 error-code, offset, and read-past-close parity is proven. Style `v-bind()` usage is discovered through the same dialect-aware planner IR, then OXC-derived `expr_roots`/`roots_complete` remain the liveness facts consumed by `mark_bindings_used_in_style` and compile-input assembly.
    53	
    54	`StyleSyntaxIr` retains positioned containment and balanced values without evaluating or compiling preprocessors. Imports, modules, plugins, guards, mixin/function arguments, and control expressions remain opaque-but-positioned.
    55	
    56	Stylesheet parser mode is deterministic by dialect and structural tokens. CSS always uses brace grammar. Sass and Stylus use the layout-capable grammar, which also recognizes explicit braced blocks. SCSS and Less use brace grammar whenever the lexer emits any plain `LeftBrace`; only a brace-free source with an actual deeper-indented line pair uses layout grammar. Closing-brace indentation and other incidental formatting never select the parser. Selector trust folds every component descendant and functional-pseudo selector list; class/ID collection descends those lists and gates each component independently, so complete literal class components may still publish from an otherwise evaluation-dependent selector such as `&.active` or `:global(.a .#{$x})`. A textually certain `:deep`/`:global`/`:slotted` kind publishes independently of argument trust, while every class inside its argument remains subject to the same per-component gate. Ambiguous optional-syntax statements remain locally typed and diagnosed without recovering intact ancestor rules. A declaration may own a retained `StyleBlock` (for example, an indented Sass nested-property namespace); the IR sink never discards such a block.
    57	
    58	**Module structure:**
    59	
    60	```
    61	style.rs              # Semantic style projection types and specificity computation
    62	style_syntax.rs       # Five-dialect syntax-to-semantic projection
    63	selector_match.rs     # Three-valued selector matching against template elements
    64	template.rs           # Template element analysis, dynamic class extraction, :style CSS var extraction
    65	```
    66	
    67	**Key types:**
    68	
    69	| Type | Location | Purpose |
    70	| ---- | -------- | ------- |
    71	| `StructuredSelector` | `style.rs` | Parsed CSS selector (compounds + combinators) |
    72	| `CompoundSelector` | `style.rs` | Single compound: element, classes, id, attributes, pseudo-classes |
    73	| `SelectorCombinator` | `style.rs` | Descendant / Child / NextSibling / LaterSibling |
    74	| `MatchResult` | `selector_match.rs` | Three-valued: `Matches`, `MaybeMatches`, `NoMatch` |
    75	| `DomQueryCallSite` | `types.rs` | DOM query call with parsed selector and spans |
    76	| `StyleBlockAnalysis` | `style.rs` | Per-`<style>` block analysis with nested `CssAnalysis` |
    77	| `AnalyzedCustomProperty` | `style.rs` | CSS custom property with name/value spans, var references, selector index |
    78	| `CssVarReference` | `style.rs` | `var()` call with name, span, optional fallback (recursive) |
    79	| `AnalyzedVarUsage` | `style.rs` | Regular CSS property using `var()` with property name and selector index |
    80	| `CssVarManipulation` | `types.rs` | Script-side CSS variable manipulation via DOM APIs |
    81	| `DynamicStyleVar` | `template.rs` | CSS variable set via `:style` binding in template |
    82	| `StaticStyleVar` | `template.rs` | CSS variable set via static `style` attribute in template |
    83	| `CssVarFlow` | `project_index.rs` | Cross-component CSS variable flow (definitions + usages + manipulations) |
    84	
    85	**CSS Variable Analysis (three-block tracking):**
    86	
    87	- **Style**: the balanced component-value IR projects `AnalyzedCustomProperty` (definitions with values/spans) and `AnalyzedVarUsage` (var() references). `extract_var_references()` handles nested var() fallbacks without evaluating values.
    88	- **Template**: `extract_dynamic_style_vars()` extracts CSS vars from `:style="{ '--color': val }"`. `extract_static_style_vars()` extracts from `style="--color: red"`.
    89	- **Script**: `try_extract_css_var_manipulation()` detects `el.style.setProperty('--x', val)`, `getPropertyValue('--x')`, `removeProperty('--x')`.
    90	- **Cross-component**: `ProjectIndex.css_var_flow(name)` and `VerterHost.css_var_flow(name)` return `CssVarFlow` with all files defining/referencing/manipulating a variable.
    91	
    92	**Selector matching algorithm** (`match_selector()`):
    93	
    94	1. Match rightmost compound against target element
    95	2. Walk left through combinators: `Child` checks `parent_index`, `Descendant` walks ancestor chain
    96	3. Dynamic `:class` or component types → `MaybeMatches` (can't determine statically)
    97	4. `:not()` inverts, `:is()`/`:where()` takes best match across alternatives
    98	
    99	**Position encoding for CSS spans**: `CssAnalysis` spans (classes, IDs, selectors) are **SFC-absolute byte offsets**. `CssSource` is constructed with the style content origin, so syntax and projection spans are absolute from creation. Consumers use spans directly without adding any offset. `StyleBlockAnalysis.content_offset` is retained for documentation and slice operations.
   100	
   101	## Analysis MCP Server (`verter_mcp`)
   102	
   103	`verter-mcp` binary exposes Verter's full analysis, diagnostics, compilation, and scoring pipeline via MCP for AI agents. `VerterMcpServer` wraps `VerterHost` (with `AnalysisScope::LSP`), `Linter`, and `ActionEngine`. Tools auto-load via `ensure_loaded()`; template analysis triggers `ensure_template_analysis()` transparently. Cross-file tools iterate all loaded files (no `ProjectIndex` exposed from host). Scoring engine computes composite 0-100 quality scores from a11y, lint, template complexity, API surface, CSS health, and reactivity dimensions.
   104	
   105	Both binaries (`verter-mcp`, and the LSP-decoupling twin `verter-mcp-server`) run the one shared entry body `verter_mcp::run::run`. The HTTP transport binds before its initial scan and announces the real bound port as a one-line stdout readiness record (`verter_mcp::readiness`, mirrored by `packages/vue-vscode/src/mcpServer.ts`); `--client-pid` arms the same `ClientProcessGuard` containment as the LSP. The VS Code extension spawns this standalone binary per LSP start attempt (`createMcpServerLifecycle`: awaited replacement, bounded crash respawn, provider-registration teardown on death) — see `docs/contributing/lsp-mcp-decoupling.md`.
   106

   166	### ScriptAnalysisSnapshot
   167	
   168	Primary output of `build_script_analysis()`. Produced by a single OXC parse + AST walk.
   169	
   170	| Field | Type | Description |
   171	| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
   172	| `imports` | `Vec<AnalyzedImport>` | All import declarations with source, bindings, spans |
   173	| `bindings` | `Vec<AnalyzedBinding>` | Top-level variable/function/class declarations |
   174	| `macros` | `Vec<AnalyzedMacro>` | Vue macro calls (defineProps, defineEmits, etc.) |
   175	| `macro_type_deps` | `Vec<MacroTypeDep>` | Cross-file type references used by macros, tiered by structural position (`usage: MacroTypeDepUsage` — `Surface` = argument root / intersection-union arms / extends heritage / alias chains, missing ⇒ error; `Member` = top-level member annotation, missing ⇒ warning + `null` degrade). References nested deeper are never collected (runtime codegen does not need them) |
   176	| `flags` | `AnalysisFlags` | Bitwise flags for O(1) queries |
   177	| `exported_functions` | `Vec<AnalyzedExportedFunction>` | Non-SFC exported functions (composable analysis). Carries `name` / `is_default` / `params` / `is_async` / `composable` only. It carries NO return-type field: the declared return type's reactive-wrapper identity is a resolution decision answered at demand time from the lowered typed IR plus a package-backed route proof (`/type-resolution` → Reactive-wrapper demand), never from annotation text on this DTO |

   179	**ReactivityKind**: None | Ref | Computed | Reactive | MaybeRef | Mutable

   198	### ProjectIndex
   199	
   200	Aggregates file-level usage into project-wide indexes:
   201	
   202	- **provide_index**: provide key → files that call `provide(key)`
   203	- **inject_index**: inject key → files that call `inject(key)`
   204	- **component_graph**: file → components it uses (forward edges)
   205	- **component_reverse_index**: component name → files that use it
   206	- **class_index**: CSS class name → files that define it
   207	- **v_bind_css_index**: v-bind CSS expression → files that use it
   208	- **custom_property_index**: CSS custom property → files that define it

   218	    |-- RawTemplateData (spans, binding refs, component tags)
   219	    |-- CssParsed* (v-bind spans, pseudo spans)

   221	    v

   223	    |-- RawTemplateData --> TemplateAnalysisSnapshot

   229	Consumers (LSP, build, linter) query snapshots + ProjectIndex
   230	```
     1	---
     2	name: compiler-codegen
     3	description: "Rust compiler pipeline, template codegen (VDOM/IDE), CodeTransform, cached directives, strict slots, IDE error recovery, style preprocessing, CompileTarget"
