  9009	## Async File Scheduler (`verter_scheduler`)
  9010	
  9011	Per-file async staging with priority queuing. Files progress independently through **Source -> Analysis -> Artifact** stages. Cross-file blocking (macro type deps, external `src`) is declarative -- the scheduler manages wakeups.
  9012	
  9013	**Key types** (`crates/verter_scheduler/src/`):
  9014	
  9015	- `FileNode` (`node.rs`) -- per-file: ArcSwap snapshots, AtomicU64 generation, pending requests
  9016	- `Scheduler` (`scheduler.rs`) -- DashMap of FileNodes, JobIndex, SubmissionInbox, driver thread
  9017	- `CompletionHandle<T>` (`job.rs`) -- request-scoped, resolves to Ready/Failed/Superseded/Shutdown
  9018	- `StageExecutor` (`executor.rs`) -- trait for plugging host parse/analysis/compile logic
  9019	- `Priority` (`stage.rs`) -- 4 tiers: Critical > Interactive > Background > Maintenance
  9020	- `EdgeManager` (`edges.rs`) -- ReverseIndex + BlockerRegistry (both DashMap-sharded)
  9021	- `OverlayMap` (`overlay.rs`) -- concurrent editor buffer storage (DashMap)
  9022	- `SourceLoader` (`source_loader.rs`) -- MemorySourceLoader (tests/WASM) + DiskSourceLoader (native)
  9023	- `IoPool` (`pool.rs`) -- bounded I/O thread pool, separate from rayon CPU pool
  9024	
  9025	### Snapshot Model
  9026	
  9027	All stage outputs are immutable `Arc`-wrapped. Replacement is atomic via ArcSwap. Generation fencing ensures coherence: `source.gen == analysis.gen == artifact.gen == node.gen`. Stale snapshots (gen mismatch) return `None` from `current_*()` methods.
  9028	
  9029	### Host Integration
  9030	
  9031	Feature-gated (`scheduler`): `VerterHost` holds an `Arc<Scheduler>`. During `upsert()`, the host submits to the scheduler, awaits the `CompletionHandle`, reads back the result, populates the compile cache. The `HostStageExecutor` calls real `parse_vue_snapshot`/`parse_non_sfc_snapshot` for the Source stage. Host-specific data is stored in snapshots via the `SnapshotData` trait (opaque `Arc<dyn Any>`), avoiding circular dependencies between scheduler and host.
  9032	
  9033	### Batch Compile & Concurrency Model (current state)
  9034	
  9035	`compile_many(inputs, CompileBatchOptions)` is the host-backed parallel SFC batch compile. Concurrency is **construction-time**, not per-call:
  9036	
  9037	- **Worker count fixed at host construction** via `HostConfig::host_cpu_threads`. The host owns a `verter_scheduler::HostCpuPool` coordinator (shared by every host batch API); never resized per call. `CompileBatchOptions` carries only `priority` + `default_mode` — there is **NO** `threads` / `thread_count` / `num_threads` field (locked by `compile_batch_options_has_no_thread_field` static guard). A per-call concurrency cap (`CpuConcurrencySemaphore`) is a Block-7 design concept, not on the tree.
  9038	- **Source upserts route through the one upsert engine.** `compile_many`'s source-updating stage calls `upsert_many_with_priority`, landing ONE `Scheduler::submit_batch_atomic` + ONE `wait_batch` for the whole batch (atomic admission — no per-file upsert fan-out).
  9039	- **Per-input requested mode, classifier-owned actual mode.** Each input carries a `requested_mode` (`CompileBatchInput.requested_mode`, defaulting to `CompileBatchOptions.default_mode` → `Session`). The `compile_cache_mode` classifier is SOLE authority for `actual_mode`: `Session` stays `Session` under every eligibility reason (its fact rail handles them); `Content` downgrades to `Stateless` on any reason (its pure key cannot represent cross-file / session-scoped input); `Stateless` is the floor. Compile dedup keyed by `(canonical, effective requested_mode)`.
  9040	- **Svelte `cssHash` override — cache identity + fail-closed content admission.** A resolved Svelte `cssHash` override (the callback is resolved OUTSIDE the compiler; only the resolved `Option<String>` threads in) is COMPILE-OUTPUT PROFILE identity, carried on `CompileProfile.svelte_css_hash_override`. It participates automatically in BOTH cache keys — `compile_profile_hash` (the session slot u64) and `content_mode_profile_hash` (the Content pure key). Because the session slot addresses on the u64 alone, `CompileOutputNodeFactValidatedSession::lookup` ALSO re-checks the exact `Option<Arc<str>>` override on the slot against the live value (`slot.css_hash_override != live` misses), so a u64 collision can never serve a result with a different scope hash ("never wrong"). A user-supplied override is not provably content-deterministic, so `classify_compile_mode` pushes `DowngradeReason::CssHashOverridePresent` when one is present ⇒ a requested `Content` compile fail-closes to `Stateless`; `Session` caching stays safe via the profile identity + the exact slot check. The override never overloads Vue's `component_id`; a static guard bans `component_id` reads from Svelte CSS hashing.
  9041	- **Session-only compile-tier prefetch.** The cold compute installs `prefetch_compile_tier_observation_targets` (cross-file import-route cache + dependency `IndexedReady` pre-population) ONLY for `actual_mode == Session`, because the compile-tier fact tracer it feeds is installed only for `Session`. `Content` / `Stateless` compile correctness (external `src=` resolution, macro-type collection, dep sync) is produced independently by `compile_entry`.
  9042	- **Target-sensitive macro demand.** `compile_entry` requests runtime, TSC, or both from the TypeInfo producer based on `CompileTarget`. Empty output still replaces the semantic transitive-dependency axis with an empty set.
  9043	- **Typed macro degradation.** Producer entries carry `Complete`, `Partial`, `Unresolved`, or `Unsupported` outcomes. The compiler accepts only a complete projection with the expected role; missing bundles, degraded entries, or role mismatches fail closed at the authored macro/type anchor. No member is silently reconstructed from parser semantics.
  9044	
  9045	### LSP Integration
  9046	
  9047	LSP file ingestion goes through the one shared upsert engine: `did_open`/`did_change` call `VerterHost::upsert` (→ `upsert_many_with_priority` → one `Scheduler::submit_batch_atomic`), which owns generation tracking, request-context propagation, post-commit cache invalidation, and the canonical-uniqueness contract. No separate LSP-side `submit_request` shim — a file is never source-updated outside the engine (the sole direct `submit_request` is `host_lifecycle.rs` disk-reload with `source: None`, a read). `compile_blockers.rs` is deprecated -- the scheduler's blocker model replaces imperative hydration.
  9048	
  9049	### Authority Chain (Final State)
  9050	
  9051	1. **Scheduler** = sole parser, raw source + analysis authority (`HostSourceData`, `HostAnalysisData`). `HostSourceData::source_type` is the authoritative `oxc_span::SourceType` for downstream cache-key sites -- computed once at `execute_source` time from the framework-neutral parse artifact (`HostSourceData::framework_parse: Option<Arc<FrameworkParseArtifact>>`, the carrier payload every host parse slot stores; Vue's `ParsedSfc` sits behind it, reachable only via the blessed `vue_parse()` accessor). Cache-key callers read via `VerterHost::authoritative_source_type_for(canonical)` or the higher-level `imported_eval_source_type_for(...)` helper.
  9052	2. **compile_cache** (`DashMap`) = profile state authority (compile_slots, overrides, diagnostics, deps, resolved_type_hashes). `CompileCacheEntry.evicted_whole_hash: Option<Hash16>` carries the pre-evict hash; `ensure_loaded` compares it to the post-reload hash and skips `bump_store_view_epoch` on no-op reloads so thread-local caches stay warm.
  9053	3. **files** (`Shared<FxHashMap>`) = WASM-only primary store. Not used on native (scheduler) path. Gated `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` / `#[cfg(any(target_arch = "wasm32", test))]` after the Phase 1 cleanup.
  9054	
  9055	Architectural target for the project-global cache overhaul:
  9056	
  9057	- scheduler remains the sole source and parse authority
  9058	- the canonical post-parse artifact above scheduler is `IndexedReady`
  9059	- `IndexedReady` owns canonical imports/exports and the owned lowered shallow symbol representation needed by later resolver work
  9060	- `AnalysisReady` should build on and enhance `IndexedReady`, not replace it with a parallel file-understanding path
  9061	- component-meta and analysis-triggered symbol expansion should populate the same host-owned resolver caches
  9062	
  9063	### Host Store View (Post-Request-View Cutover)
  9064	
  9065	The `CURRENT_REQUEST_VIEW` thread-local, `EffectiveView`, and `*_in_view` helpers are retired; `RequestStoreView` (`crates/verter_session/src/resolver_core/request_store_view.rs`) itself remains a live `pub(crate)` overlay `StoreView`. Resolver-path helpers take `&HostStoreView` (or use the host's live probes directly). `HostStoreView::from_host(self)` snapshots a cheap immutable view of the host's current state; its cache-validation identity is the complete `StoreViewValidationToken`, while `StoreView::compat_token` returns the narrower `StoreViewCompatToken` lane identity (epoch + session + `validity_fingerprint` = the external-supersession fold) — see "Store-View Token, Lane Identity, and Singleflight" below.
  9066	
  9067	Key rules:
  9068	
  9069	- Resolver-path helpers read state directly from the host and `ProjectTypeStore`. No request-private extension store — canonicals loaded mid-request via `ensure_loaded` publish to `ProjectTypeStore` / `FileArtifactStore` and become visible to all readers.
  9070	- `VerterHost::is_evalable(canonical)` is the canonical shallow-probe API; it calls `get_whole_hash(canonical).is_some()` directly.
  9071	- `ensure_loaded` publishes to the scheduler + `FileArtifactStore`; no extension-store plumbing.
  9072	- Cache-validation staleness is enforced by the `ReadSetSignature.facts` path-precise fact signature on cache entries. Warm hits revalidate every recorded fact against the live `StoreView` before returning; stale entries miss and force a cold rebuild.
  9073	- Host-scoped caches (final `ComponentMetaResultDb`, `OwnerImportSurfaceDb`, `SemanticGraphStore`) validate through dep-signatures; transient `TypeSurfaceDb` writes only happen through `publish_with_facts` which attaches dep-signatures.
  9074	
  9075	Native canonical loading goes through `ensure_loaded` — the scheduler is the sole source authority. Disk-read fall-throughs were deleted on native. WASM keeps the `files` map + workspace fallback.
  9076	
  9077	### Store-View Token, Lane Identity, and Singleflight
  9078	
  9079	`HostStoreView` is Arc-backed by an immutable `StoreViewSnapshot`: `VerterHost::store_view_manager()` hands out ONE shared snapshot per `StoreViewValidationToken` generation by cheap `Arc` clone; `with_session_overlay` re-roots overlay/tombstone canonicals via copy-on-write so the shared base is never mutated in place. `RequestStoreView` (`resolver_core::request_store_view`) is the LIVE request-scoped read-through wrapper: it chains a `CanonicalCompletionOverlay` in front of the request-entry `HostStoreView` so mid-request additive loads (`ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` successes the entry snapshot did not track) validate without a false miss. The `CanonicalCompletionOverlay` also carries the request-world prepared-decl bundle memo (`RequestBundleMemo`, reached through `CanonicalCompletionOverlay::bundle_memo()` and threaded explicitly into `prepared_decl_bundle_with_store_view` / consulted by `prepared_decl_bundle_with_context` via `ResolverContext::request_completion_overlay`). It is ONE memo covering the base, session-overlay and `RequestOnly` worlds, keyed `(canonical, BundleMemoWorld)` with the `StoreViewCompatToken` on the entry: `BundleMemoWorld::{Base, Overlay(content hash)}` keeps the base and session namespaces distinct (R17 keeps overlay-bearing bundles OUT of the shared `prepared_decl_bundles` cache, and the shared slot is keyed by canonical alone), while the token pins entries to ONE externally-coherent world so a stability-retry attempt under an externally-moved view misses and re-materialises. Admission is STRUCTURAL: `RequestBundleMemo::insert` itself refuses anything that is not `ReuseClass::is_request_reusable`, so a cancelled, partial, lease-missed, mutation-unstable or overflow-refused materialisation never enters it, and a `RequestOnly` entry replays its stored refusal on EVERY hit so reuse cannot launder the taint (provenance counter `bundle_request_memo_hits`; regressions in `crates/verter_session/src/request_bundle_memo_tests.rs`).
  9080	
  9081	**Reuse/validity oracle = the complete `StoreViewValidationToken`:** `store_view_epoch` + `project_generation` + `FileArtifactStore.artifact_generation` + `load_generation` + the workspace `content_generation` + folded env hashes + project identity + frozen overlay identity. `store_view_epoch` is an INPUT to the token, not the oracle by itself. Token-advance rules — the token advances on EVERY state change a base view snapshots by value:
  9082	
  9083	- Every `FileArtifactStore` keyed insert/replace/evict/GC/per-canonical-retention sweep and every augmentation-index mutation bumps `artifact_generation`. `IndexedReady` is the single per-file artifact: route facts come from the current-content `IndexedReady` surface (no separate route-owned artifact), gated by `indexed_surface_is_current` (edge currency + the `project_generation` stamp for surfaces with cross-file edges; a route-resolution mutation drives an edge-refresh materialise that reuses the content-addressed payload and rebuilds the route surface).
  9084	- A successful FIRST-TIME additive `ensure_loaded` bumps the dedicated `load_generation` (as does a positive import-route admission via `cache_positive_import_route_result`): it adds a scheduler node + `derived_raw_cache` state the build folds into `whole_hashes`/`derived_hashes` but does NOT publish into `FileArtifactStore`, so `artifact_generation` alone would not cover it. It deliberately does NOT bump `store_view_epoch` — a cold compute's own dependency loads stay EXCLUDED from the publish fence's `externally_superseded_by` check and never self-fence promotion.
  9085	
  9086	**Singleflight LANE identity is NARROWER than the reuse oracle.** The coalescing-lane identity is `StoreViewCompatToken`, whose `validity_fingerprint` is the `lane_fingerprint` — delegating to `external_supersession_fingerprint`, the SAME oracle the promotion fence `is_stable` applies. The fingerprint folds ONLY the external-supersession dimensions: `store_view_epoch` + `project_generation` + workspace `content_generation` (file-set mutations — watcher recovery / dependency appearance — advance it without any host-side epoch; a snapshot's edge-currency gates evaluate against it at build time, so a cached snapshot MUST miss once it moves; a cold compute's own loads never advance it, so it cannot self-fence) + folded env hashes (`env_hash_fold`) + `project_identity` + frozen overlay identity. The additive generations (`artifact_generation` / `load_generation`) are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the lane identity: a cold compute advances them through its OWN work (materialising content-addressed caches gated by `store_view_epoch`, loading its dependencies, admitting its own routes), so two identical concurrent requests snapshot at slightly different points in the load sweep — folding those generations would split them across separate lanes and spawn multiple cold winners instead of one leader + N-1 dedup-joining followers. Because the lane oracle IS the promotion oracle, a follower that joins a lane shares exactly the external dimensions the leader's promotion was gated on, so the leader's dedup-joined result is validation-equivalent for it; and a request whose snapshot externally-supersedes the leader's (an epoch / project / env / identity / overlay change, even at an equal `store_view_epoch`) gets a different lane key and forks its own lane — it never receives a result computed under a different external view. The complete `StoreViewValidationToken` (including the additive generations) REMAINS the store-view reuse/validity oracle — the `StoreViewManager` rebuilds its base snapshot on any additive-generation change; only the LANE identity was narrowed (reuse-oracle = full token; lane-identity = external fingerprint).
  9087	
  9088	**Base-view build:** no-torn-return (a coherent capture or `Superseded`, never a torn publishable view) and SINGLEFLIGHTED — on a token miss exactly one caller sweeps while concurrent token-miss callers wait on a condvar and clone the winner's `Arc<StoreViewSnapshot>` (no N-way parallel sweeps). The component-meta cold publish fence rechecks the computed-under token against the live host before promotion (mismatch → return-only, no shared-cache warm), keying off `externally_superseded_by` so the compute's OWN artifact publications do not self-fence.
  9089	
  9090	**Captured resolution root (C5a).** The snapshot also stamps the workspace's immutable published resolution world (`Option<Arc<verter_workspace::CapturedResolutionWorld>>`, captured O(1) in the same `PreBuildTokenInputs` read window via `WorkspaceRead::capture_resolution_world`: the current base root plus, for a session population, that session's overlay root). It is the SOLE authority for the `ResolveImportsFactRef::Resolution` arm — `HostStoreView::validates_resolution_fact` (shared by `validates_resolve_imports_domain` and its overlay-aware `_for_content_hash` sibling; `RequestStoreView` routes resolution facts straight to the base view because the completion overlay carries no resolver observations). A view with NO captured world validates no resolution fact. It stays OUT of the token because validity is fact-precise (world IDENTITY is barred from being a cross-root warm-validity oracle) and because a cold compute publishes replacement worlds through its OWN work (a first observation of any path records an evidence baseline), which would self-fence exactly like the additive generations. Residual, owned by C4/C5b: a view captured between a content mutation and the reader-driven evidence refresh holds a root that has not yet observed the change, so it keeps validating the pre-mutation witness until the refresh advances the fact.
  9091	
  9092	**Handle-backed dimensions stay out of the token for DIFFERENT reasons:** `ResolvedImportFactsDb` is content-addressed — its key carries `content_hash`, so a new version is a new key and a fixed handle reads correctly (immutable-by-key). `RouteDb` is NOT content-addressed (its keys carry no content hash, and evict/clear/replace reuse the same key) — it stays out because every value it hands out is validated per candidate against the reading view through the candidate's own recorded `fact_dep_signature`, so an evict/replace yields a conservative fail-closed MISS, never a stale positive. The per-candidate signature comparison IS the validity rail, so the token needs no `RouteDb` generation. The route-surface FACT domain does not read `RouteDb` at all: its sole arm (`StoreView::validates_route_surface_domain`) compares the recorded `expected_hash` against the augmentation-index fingerprint snapshot captured on the view's artifact root.
  9093	
  9094	### Non-Current Store-View Contract — Capability Split (CRITICAL)
  9095	
  9096	The general store-view accessor `VerterHost::resolver_store_view()` returns the capability-split `StoreViewRead`, never a raw `HostStoreView`. The raw unwrap that erased the non-current proof is gone: every caller must compile-choose one of two capabilities, so no caller can validate (warm) or return (query) against a known-stale snapshot by accident.
  9097	
  9098	- `StoreViewRead::current()` → `CurrentHostStoreView` — the `StoreViewManager` proved this view current at handoff. Allowed for warm-cache fact validation AND for returning a normal query result.
  9099	- `StoreViewRead::into_cold_seed_view()` → `ColdSeedHostStoreView` — usable ONLY for a fenced cold builder. It exposes NO `validates*` surface, so a stale seed cannot reach a fact validator by construction. It carries the read's currentness so a derived context fails closed.
  9100	
  9101	Concrete contract:
  9102	
  9103	- **Warm validators require `&CurrentHostStoreView`.** The top-level warm-validation entry points with no outer publish fence (`try_get_cached_meta_payload`, `ComponentMetaResultDb::get_with_view`, the imported-root / owner-import-surface warm reads) accept ONLY a proven-current view. A `ReturnOnly` read is a cache MISS, not a validation — the caller falls to the cold path whose own `is_stable` / publish fence gates promotion.
  9104	- **typeinfo query-returners do bounded-retry-then-supersede.** `resolve_named_symbol`, `evaluate_type_expression`, `project_node_to_type_expr_json_bytes` (the session-owned bytes FFI facade that mints the `OutputProjector` capability + materializes + serializes internally), `resolve_shallow_surface`, `resolve_vue_macro_surface`, `resolve_vue_public_type`, and `resolve_type_with_audit` build a request-bound dispatch context and RETURN the resolved node with NO outer fence. They acquire a `CurrentHostStoreView` via `typeinfo::current_store_view_for_query` (bounded retry, default 3); on sustained churn they surface a typed non-current MISS (`None`, or `QueryError::UnstableState`) rather than resolving against a superseded snapshot and returning a stale node. `None` is the established FFI miss signal (`typeExpr: null`). The retry is bounded — it terminates, never spins. A non-current evaluation must NOT warm the `scratch_cache`.
  9105	- **Every branch of a cache-presence-selected lane binds a REQUEST-BOUND context.** `VerterHost::build_template_class_semantic_facts` (`host_manage/analysis_io.rs`) picks its resolver context from artifact presence: the base-publishable + `IndexedReady`-present branch builds a `HostResolverContext::from_cold_seed`, the other composes a `SessionResolverContext::from_cold_seed`. The resolver-tier builder takes `&dyn RequestBoundResolverContext` — the sealed marker implemented for those two contexts and NEVER for `VerterHost` — so a bare-host binding is a COMPILE error, not a cache-presence-dependent runtime abort. The rail matters because `classify_binding` demands `prepared_value_decl` for every template `:class` script binding, and only a request-bound context can serve a prepared declaration. Regression: `template_class_lane_context_tests.rs` (indexed-present assertion + cold-seed control).
  9106	- **Cold contexts carry `Current` vs `ColdSeed`.** `HostResolverContext::from_current(&CurrentHostStoreView)` vs `HostResolverContext::from_cold_seed(&ColdSeedHostStoreView)` — and the session-bound counterpart `SessionResolverContext::from_cold_seed(&ColdSeedHostStoreView)`. The cold-seed constructor marks the request-bound `RequestStoreView` non-current iff the seed was `ReturnOnly`; its `validates*` family then fails CLOSED, so every nested warm-cache probe inside the dispatch MISSES rather than validating against the stale seed. This is the single-chokepoint enforcement — no individual nested validator knows about currentness.
  9107	- **Cold-seed currentness is INTRINSIC to its read — never a separately-sourced flag.** A cold-seed view's `is_current` comes from the SAME read that produced its raw view: `StoreViewRead::into_cold_seed_view()` derives it from the read's arm (`Current` vs `ReturnOnly`). There is no constructor that pairs a raw view with a caller-supplied bool — the retired `ColdSeedHostStoreView::from_raw_for_compute(view, separate_flag)` was exactly such a footgun, letting a view from one read be re-bound with a currentness flag from ANOTHER read (a stale second read marked current). Two valid sources of a cold-seed in a validating cold compute:
  9108	  - **A helper that does its OWN fresh read** takes the cold-seed straight from that read: `self.resolver_store_view_read().into_cold_seed_view()` (then `.with_session_overlay(..)` for the session path). The view-bound component-meta cold compute (`VerterHost::view_bound_cold_seed` → `compute_component_meta_state_with_view` / `_from_captured_with_view`) and the bare-host overlay entries (`compute_component_meta_state_with_overlay` / `_from_captured_with_overlay`) use this — currentness and view come from one read, no flag to mismatch.
  9109	  - **A helper that holds the EXECUTOR's single-read `(view, is_current)` pair** re-binds it via the SOLE pairing constructor `StoreViewRead::from_executor_snapshot(view, is_current)` (returns the intrinsic-currentness enum, consumed via `.into_cold_seed_view()`), confined to the executor boundary where the pair provably came from one read. The fallthrough cold compute (`compute_fallthrough_surface_uncached`) and the component-meta `*_with_view_arg` entries use this — the executor's `snapshot_view` destructured one `StoreViewRead` and threaded both into `compute`. The executors (`ComponentMetaRequestExecutor`, `FallthroughRequestExecutor`) track `snapshot_view_current` and thread it into `compute(.., base_is_current)`.
  9110	- **The cold-seed escape hatch (`ColdSeedHostStoreView::into_inner`) never feeds a validating context (INDIRECT-validation seam).** The raw unwrap `.into_cold_seed_view().into_inner()` DROPS the `is_current` flag. It is confined to NON-validating consumers: the request-driver `snapshot_store_view()` accessors, the overlay-priority `capture_component_meta_inputs_with_view` (builds `CapturedComponentMetaInputs` only), and `#[cfg(test)]` direct-`host` wrappers. The fallthrough resolver validates its per-element / per-child / per-root node-cache entries through the request-bound `ctx.store_view()` (currentness-gated), not a separately-rebuilt raw `HostStoreView`.
  9111	- **Fenced cold seeds remain correct.** A real fenced cold builder (`cold_seed_view_and_fence` + `ColdSeedFence`, the request-driver `compute` path) may compute from a `ReturnOnly` coherent seed to avoid blocking, but re-checks currentness before publishing: a non-current seed's result is non-cacheable and surfaces as superseded/degraded, never warmed into the shared cache. Cold builders are NOT forced to `Current` (that would needlessly block cold progress under churn).
  9112	- **The raw-view escape hatch is allowlisted.** `StoreViewRead::into_owned_view()` yields a raw `HostStoreView` ONLY for the bare-host owned-view rail (`ResolverContext::resolver_store_view`, reachable when no request-bound context was installed), the request-driver owned-view snapshot accessors (currentness gated by `snapshot_view_is_current`), and `.into_cold_seed_view().into_inner()` fenced cold seeds.
  9113	
  9114	Pinned by the static guards in `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/architecture_guards.rs`: `resolver_store_view_returns_store_view_read` (return type is `StoreViewRead`), `cold_seed_store_view_exposes_no_validation_surface` (no `validates*` on `ColdSeedHostStoreView`), `warm_validation_entry_points_require_current_store_view` (warm validators keep `&CurrentHostStoreView`), `resolver_store_view_into_owned_view_is_allowlisted` (raw-view escape hatch confined to the allowlist), `cold_seed_into_inner_confined_to_non_validating_allowlist` (the `into_cold_seed_view().into_inner()` raw-unwrap that drops currentness is confined to non-validating consumers — the INDIRECT-validation seam), `cold_compute_context_constructors_carry_currentness` (cold-compute context constructors are the currentness-carrying `from_cold_seed` form rooted on `RequestStoreView::new_cold_seed`; the footgun `from_raw_for_compute` stays retired; `from_executor_snapshot` is the sole executor-boundary re-bind), and `cold_seed_currentness_is_intrinsic_to_the_read` (the `(view, flag)` re-bind `from_executor_snapshot` is confined to the executor-boundary allowlist, and a fresh `resolver_store_view_read()` may never feed it — closing the view+flag divergence the constructor-shape guards missed), plus the discriminating regressions in `crates/verter_session/src/store_view_non_current_contract_tests.rs` (`session_cold_seed_context_fails_warm_probes_closed`, `view_bound_cold_seed_currentness_comes_from_its_own_read`, `fallthrough_cold_compute_node_cache_validation_fails_closed_under_churn`).

  9141	### Template class fact lanes
  9142	
  9143	Normal compile, content override, and lazy raw-template conversion must all
  9144	build `TemplateClassSemanticFacts` from the exact source `whole_hash` and the
  9145	same script snapshot used by conversion. `CompileInput` and
  9146	`VueTemplateInputs` carry that hash. Base-current computations may retain
  9147	complete facts only with their validated dependency `ReadSetSignature`;
  9148	overlay, missing/cyclic, or otherwise `ReturnOnly` computations never populate
  9149	base-only caches. Content publication is owner-only, so dependency-derived
  9150	class facts are served fresh without entering the pure-content store.
  9151	
  9152	`template_converter_inputs` is linkage-only. Semantic class domains flow
  9153	through the opaque, revision-checked `TemplateClassDomainIndex`; callers must
  9154	not manufacture raw class-domain tuples or recover domains from display text.

  9383	   208	/// Detect routing framework from package.json content string.
  9384	   209	pub fn detect_routing_framework_from_json(content: &str) -> RoutingFramework {

  9391	   216	        json.get("dependencies").and_then(|d| d.get(name)).is_some()
  9392	   217	            || json

  9394	   219	                .and_then(|d| d.get(name))

  9402	   227	        RoutingFramework::UnpluginVueRouter

  9404	   229	        RoutingFramework::VueRouter
  9405	   230	    } else {
  9406	   231	        RoutingFramework::Unknown
  9407	   232	    }
  9408	   233	}

 10025	   607	/// Mutating view of the workspace authority — extends [`WorkspaceRead`]
 10026	   608	/// with edge recording, exact-resolution writes, overlay notifications,
 10027	   609	/// audit-sink registry, and ambient-lib mutators.
 10028	   610	///
 10029	   611	/// All workspace I/O (reads, writes, walks, resolution) goes through this
 10030	   612	/// trait hierarchy. There is no separate `ProjectResolverReader` or
 10031	   613	/// `ConfigFileReader`. The resolver, config parser, and host all take
 10032	   614	/// `&dyn WorkspaceAccess` (or the narrower `&dyn WorkspaceRead` for
 10033	   615	/// read-only consumers).
 10034	   616	///
 10035	   617	/// # Implementors
 10036	   618	///
 10037	   619	/// - [`FilesystemWorkspace`] — disk-backed with overlay/snapshot cache
 10038	   620	/// - [`MemoryWorkspace`] — fully in-memory (tests, WASM, playground)
 10039	   621	/// - Lightweight adapters (LSP readers) that delegate to a host's workspace
 10040	   622	///
 10041	   623	/// # sub-
 10042	   624	///
 10043	   625	/// `WorkspaceAccess` is no longer the public read API for external crates;
 10044	   626	/// it is gated behind `pub(crate) VerterHost::workspace()`. Read consumers
 10045	   627	/// outside `verter_session` use `VerterHost::workspace_read()` →
 10046	   628	/// `Arc<dyn WorkspaceRead>`. Mutators (`notify_close`, `notify_upsert`,
 10047	   629	/// `set_exact_resolutions`, `configure_resolver`) are reachable only via
 10048	   630	/// host wrappers that run the cache-cascade discipline.
 10049	   631	pub trait WorkspaceAccess: WorkspaceRead {
 10050	   632	    /// Open and close a strict-self-root authority write bracket. Backends
 10051	   633	    /// that expose a generation override these together with the active-
 10052	   634	    /// writer read above.
 10053	   635	    fn begin_strict_self_root_transition(&self) {}
 10054	   636	
 10055	   637	    fn end_strict_self_root_transition(&self) {}
 10056	   638	
 10057	   639	    // ── Reverse-graph authority methods (R6: NO DEFAULTS) ──
 10058	   640	    //
 10059	   641	    // Every WorkspaceAccess impl MUST explicitly implement these. A future
 10060	   642	    // impl that forgets to override would have silently dropped edges under
 10061	   643	    // a default-no-op design; R6's compile-time enforcement makes that
 10062	   644	    // impossible.

 10491	    90	## 1.4 Simplicity
 10492	    91	
 10493	    92	Every service object, trait, cache, lock, queue, actor, version, background task, and cross-crate boundary must prove why a direct function, immutable value, private owner, or request-local calculation is insufficient.
 10494	    93	
 10495	    94	Preference order:
 10496	    95	
 10497	    96	```text
 10498	    97	pure function
 10499	    98	-> borrowed/request-local value
 10500	    99	-> immutable value object
 10501	   100	-> small private owner
 10502	   101	-> reusable query when cross-request reuse or validation is valuable
 10503	   102	-> executor task when work is coarse and independent
 10504	   103	-> actor when a stateful external protocol/resource requires serialized ownership
 10505	   104	```
 10506	   105	
 10507	   106	A one-implementation public trait is rejected unless it is a real substitution boundary. A new crate is rejected unless it establishes a dependency firewall, stable protocol, or multiple credible consumers.
 10508	   107	
 10509	   108	## 1.5 Constitutional invariants and evidence-selected tactics
 10510	   109	
 10511	   110	Revision 11 is the strongest defensible target under current evidence, not a claim of globally proven optimality before implementation. `contracts/architecture-falsification.md` classifies decisions as constitutional invariants, repository/product facts, evidence-selected tactics, or deferred research choices.
 10512	   111	
 10513	   112	Constitutional rules—such as one semantic authority, honest completeness, direct/managed separation, deterministic products, bounded lifetime, and one-path cutovers—cannot be weakened locally. Repository facts are refreshed against the exact checkout. Private tactics may change when measurements disprove them, provided public semantics, ownership, failure behavior, compatibility, and locked gates remain intact. Deferred research does not enter a candidate through speculative “future proofing.”
 10514	   113	
 10515	   114	A6 accepts an architecture premise ledger. Falsified premises stop affected work, preserve independently valid work, and trigger refresh, rescope, or ADR amendment according to their class.
 10516	   115	
 10517	   400	1. **Native threaded:** bounded structured CPU execution and owner-affine workers.
 10518	   401	2. **Native single-thread:** identical semantics with inline/local execution and no unnecessary concurrent containers.
 10519	   402	3. **WASM single-thread:** local/cooperative execution, non-`Send` stores, and no dependency on blocking condvars or native worker pools.
 10520	   403	
 10521	   404	Optional future WASM threads form a separate capability and do not redefine the single-thread contract.
 10522	   405	
 10523	   406	`QueryRuntime` semantics—identity, completeness, validation, cancellation, recursion, and admission—are independent from how a profile schedules work.

 10525	   408	# 5. Input authority and snapshots
 10526	   409	
 10527	   410	## 5.1 One committed input authority
 10528	   411	
 10529	   412	The managed system has exactly one authority for committed sources, overlays, project topology, and configuration. `InputStore` is the logical role; Revision 11 does not require inventing a new type when the current registered-source/VFS/`PublishedRoot` machinery already owns the invariant and can be converged in place.
 10530	   413	
 10531	   414	The required invariant is:
 10532	   415	
 10533	   416	> A reader observes one coherent source/project/configuration state before a commit or after it, never independently sampled roots from different commits.
 10534	   417	
 10535	   418	An immutable/persistent root published through a short atomic commit is preferred. Equivalent implementations are allowed only if they preserve coherent capture, ordered document mutation, conditional commit, short writer critical sections, bounded memory, and deterministic snapshot identity.
 10536	   419	
 10537	   420	No parse, compile, TypeInfo, provider, index, cache validation, or external I/O runs inside the input write critical section.
 10538	   421	
 10539	   422	Before managed QueryRuntime/cache convergence, the current input/VFS/publication owner is classified and its snapshot/fact API is locked. Query infrastructure must not be built around a transitional or independently sampled source view.
 10540	   423	
 10541	   424	## 5.2 Ordered document mutation
 10542	   425	
 10543	   426	For each document:
 10544	   427	
 10545	   428	- accepted incremental edits are applied in order;
 10546	   429	- incarnation and document version are validated;
 10547	   430	- edits are never dropped or coalesced before source application;
 10548	   431	- derived work may be cancelled/coalesced after commit;
 10549	   432	- an invalid range/version gap enters an explicit unsynchronized state;
 10550	   433	- a later range is never applied to unproven text.
 10551	   434	
 10552	   435	## 5.3 Lazy input loading
 10553	   436	
 10554	   437	Reusable semantic/compiler computation performs no unversioned filesystem, network, package-manager, or process read behind a snapshot. Missing information is resolved by the deterministic state machine in `contracts/input-loading.md`.
 10555	   438	
 10556	   439	At a high level:
 10557	   440	
 10558	   441	```text
 10559	   442	Attempt(snapshot, accumulated observations, resource budget)
 10560	   443	  -> Complete(result)
 10561	   444	  -> NeedInputs(normalized LoadSet)
 10562	   445	  -> TerminalFailure
 10563	   446	```
 10564	   447	
 10565	   448	For `NeedInputs`:
 10566	   449	
 10567	   450	1. normalize, sort, and deduplicate the complete discovered set for the attempt;
 10568	   451	2. compute `delta = requested - previously_requested`;
 10569	   452	3. fail with typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` when `delta` is empty and no observed basis changed;
 10570	   453	4. enforce total unique-input, byte, dependency-depth, retry, and churn budgets;
 10571	   454	5. load `delta` through same-key I/O flights owned outside the semantic kernel;
 10572	   455	6. conditionally commit successful and stable negative observations as one coherent batch when the project/configuration basis is still current;
 10573	   456	7. capture a new snapshot and restart the whole semantic attempt;
 10574	   457	8. never splice newly loaded data into an in-progress derivation.
 10575	   458	
 10576	   459	A basis change may justify a retry even with the same symbolic dependency, but it consumes the configured churn/restart budget. Partial load success, stable missing observations, and transient loader failures have distinct typed outcomes.
 10577	   460	
 10578	   461	`TypeInfoEnvironment` is an immutable/data-only observation view. Public/external environments provide bytes and typed metadata, not authoritative semantic fingerprints: Verter validates key/basis consistency and computes or verifies content/configuration fingerprints at the capture boundary. A caller-supplied digest is a hint unless it was minted by a sealed first-party snapshot authority and carries its validity basis. A direct project session returns `NeedInputs` to its caller; a managed embedding may run the outer load/commit/retry loop. The compiler and semantic kernel remain I/O-free.
 10579	   462	
 10580	   463	# 6. Parsing, source units, and artifacts
 10581	   464	
 10582	   465	## 6.1 Shared frontend, parse key, and owner domain
 10583	   466	
 10584	   467	For each language domain, Verter owns one error-tolerant syntax frontend used by IDE and build:
 10585	   468	
 10586	   469	- Vue carrier;
 10587	   470	- Svelte carrier;
 10588	   558	-> admitted managed artifact when measured cross-request reuse is valuable
 10589	   559	-> optional persistent artifact only when hermetic eligibility is proven
 10590	   560	```
 10591	   561	
 10592	   562	Correct computation does not imply admission. Return-only results are normal.

 10594	   564	# 7. Direct compiler, plans, and compile projections
 10595	   565	
 10596	   566	## 7.1 Direct compiler boundary
 10597	   567	
 10598	   568	The direct compiler is a separate product boundary, not an `Engine` mode. It exposes borrowed-source one-shot compilation, explicit prepared reuse, and staged batch planning/emission. It owns no workspace, committed input store, QueryRuntime, provider lifecycle, durable cache set, audit database, or background scheduler.
 10599	   569	
 10600	   570	No public `dyn CompileTypeInfo`, open resolver trait, `Engine`, `VerterHost`, provider state, or ambient filesystem handle enters the direct compiler.
 10601	   571	
 10602	   572	## 7.2 Typed operation plan
 10603	   573	
 10604	   574	The compiler consumes the final compositional request and derives the smallest acyclic prerequisite closure. A cold request plans once by default. Deliberate replanning is allowed only when benchmark evidence shows it is cheaper in total CPU, allocation, retained memory, and complexity than carrying the first plan.
 10605	   575	
 10606	   576	Unsupported product combinations fail before expensive work. No projection demands means zero TypeInfo construction/call and zero project read.
 10607	   577	
 10608	   578	## 7.3 Resumable projection protocol
 10609	   579	
 10610	   580	Project-aware compilation follows:
 10611	   581	
 10612	   582	```text
 10613	   583	prepare -> plan -> project -> emit
 10614	   584	```
 10615	   585	
 10616	   586	Conceptually:
 10617	   587	
 10618	   588	```rust
 10619	   589	let mut prepared = compiler.prepare(source_id, source, parse_options)?;
 10620	   590	let plan = prepared.plan(request)?;
 10621	   591	
 10622	   592	loop {
 10623	   593	    match type_info.project(plan.projection_batch())? {
 10624	   594	        ProjectionOutcome::Complete(facts) => {
 10625	   595	            plan.validate_facts(&facts)?;
 10626	   596	            break prepared.emit(plan, facts);
 10627	   597	        }
 10628	   598	        ProjectionOutcome::NeedInputs(load_set) => {
 10629	   599	            return CompileAttempt::NeedInputs {
 10630	   600	                prepared,
 10631	   601	                plan,
 10632	   602	                load_set,
 10633	   603	            };
 10634	   604	        }
 10635	   605	    }
 10636	   606	}
 10637	   607	```
 10638	   608	
 10639	   609	The exact Rust API may use separate types/builders. The invariants are binding:
 10640	   610	
 10641	   611	- `CompileProjectionBatch` is compact, owned, and OXC-free;
 10642	   612	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized per-product request to the retained prepared root for anti-replay;
 10643	   613	- the plan also contains narrower deterministic `ProjectionPlanToken`, product-subplan tokens, and terminal-subplan tokens, so a terminal-only change does not invalidate unchanged semantic/code artifacts;
 10644	   614	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds to the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`, semantic profile, dependency/input basis, and completeness—not to unrelated presentation or serialization fields;
 10645	   615	- stale, replayed, mismatched, or injected facts are rejected before emission;
 10646	   616	- no AST borrow, arena pointer, or unvalidated locator crosses external I/O;
 10647	   617	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a first-class resumable outcome, not a generic internal error;
 10648	   618	- the outer caller may extend a captured project view and retry under the load-wave/no-progress contract;
 10649	   619	- a project/configuration basis change invalidates/replans as specified by the token rather than silently reusing facts.
 10650	   620	
 10651	   621	One-shot convenience APIs may orchestrate local-only semantics synchronously. Project-capable convenience orchestration must remain explicit about loading and retry; compute itself stays I/O-free.
 10652	   622	
 10653	   623	## 7.4 Sealed `CompileTypeInfo`
 10654	   624	
 10655	   625	```rust
 10656	   626	pub struct CompileTypeInfo<'env> {
 10657	   627	    inner: CompileTypeInfoInner<'env>,
 10658	   628	}
 10659	   629	```
 10660	   630	
 10661	   631	All first-party local, captured-project, in-memory, engine-snapshot, and validated-precomputed modes execute one `TypeInfoCore`, one `ModuleResolverCore`, and one profile-parameterized relation/inference implementation. External integrations supply captured data observations, not resolution/type/classification semantics.
 10662	   632	
 10663	   633	No blanket `Send + Sync` applies. Parallel batches use staged prepare/plan, one TypeInfo owner with internal parallelism or explicit first-party per-worker sessions, and parallel emit when legal.
 10664	   634	
 10665	   635	Validated precomputed facts are optional and accepted only after domain/profile/toolchain/source/dependency/completeness/integrity/size and anti-replay validation. Callers cannot mint arbitrary resolved facts.
 10666	   636	
 10667	   637	## 7.5 Closed framework projections
 10668	   638	
 10669	   639	The compiler discovers exact closed projection demands. Vue runtime macro projection contains only facts runtime generation consumes: prop/model identity, optional/required/default association, ordered broad runtime constructors, `skip_check`/typed degradation, provenance anchor, and exact dependency/profile basis.
 10670	   640	
 10671	   641	Projection follows imports, aliases, substitutions, unions/intersections, utility/mapped/indexed forms, `typeof`, enums, and supported forms only until the closed answer is known. Object internals are not expanded merely to conclude `Object`.
 10672	   642	
 10673	   643	Current Svelte runtime compilation requests no native compile projection unless a future capability ADR proves an official semantic need.
 10674	   644

 10990	    26	## 2. The locked strategy
 10991	    27	
 10992	    28	**One `cargo metadata`-driven forbidden-edge test over the whole workspace graph, modelled
 10993	    29	exactly on `verter_macro_dto`'s `dependency_closure_guard`. No new source-text scanner.**
 10994	    30	
 10995	    31	This is not a stylistic preference; it follows from `CLAUDE.md`'s forward-only rule: *landed*
 10996	    32	enforcement is compiler/type-system/tool-based and never a name/text/grep scanner over the source
 10997	    33	tree. Three of the four mechanisms above are exactly the scanner form that rule grandfathers but
 10998	    34	forbids extending. The fourth is the model to generalise, and it is already the better test on the
 10999	    35	merits:
 11000	    36	
 11001	    37	- it reads what cargo actually links, so a forbidden edge added **behind any feature**, or
 11002	    38	  arriving **transitively**, fails — a manifest scan sees none of those;
 11003	    39	- it distinguishes production edges (normal + build) from dev-dependencies, so a guard's own
 11004	    40	  tooling dev-deps cannot self-trip it;
 11005	    41	- it pins its sanctioned exception by **equality** against a structurally computed set, so an
 11006	    42	  upstream release that grows the exception is a re-audit gate rather than a silent grant.
 11007	    43	
 11008	    44	Naming crates in a layer matrix is not the scanner failure mode the rule forbids. The rule's
 11009	    45	target is text matching over source; a resolve-graph walk over cargo's own output is the
 11010	    46	"real used tool" form it prescribes. The matrix is data for a graph query, not a grep pattern.

 11012	    48	### 2.1 Required properties of the `B1` test
 11013	    49	
 11014	    50	1. **Input** — `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features`, the resolve cargo builds from.
 11015	    51	2. **Edges** — normal + build, transitive. Dev edges excluded and that exclusion stated.
 11016	    52	3. **Assertion form** — for each crate, its production closure must not reach any crate in a
 11017	    53	   strictly higher layer. Closure-based, not direct-edge-based: a direct-edge test passes while a
 11018	    54	   two-hop violation walks straight through it (§4 shows this is not hypothetical).
 11019	    55	4. **Exceptions** — equality-pinned, never subset-checked, each with a recorded rationale.
 11020	    56	5. **Discrimination** — the test must FAIL when a forbidden edge is added. `B1` proves it by
 11021	    57	   adding one to a scratch manifest and observing the failure, and the proof must show the
 11022	    58	   mutation was actually applied (`CLAUDE.md` → Verification Must Prove Execution: a plant that
 11023	    59	   fails to apply reports a pass).
 11024	    60	6. **Supersession, with one residue that must be decided rather than assumed.** Landing the
 11025	    61	   closure test deletes `verter_audit_no_upward_deps` and both tests in `no_session_dep.rs`:
 11026	    62	   their invariants are strictly implied by the walk (`verter_audit` closure ⊆
 11027	    63	   {`verter_audit`, `verter_span`}; `verter_scheduler` closure excludes `verter_session`), and
 11028	    64	   a source path reference to a non-dependency crate does not compile, so the source-scan half
 11029	    65	   adds nothing a closure walk misses. Keeping them would be a second authority for one rule,
 11030	    66	   and deleting them in the same accepted candidate is `CLAUDE.md`'s clean-cutover requirement.
 11031	    67	
 11032	    68	   `audit_substrate_isolation` is **not** fully implied, and `B1` must not delete it on the
 11033	    69	   assumption that it is. Its *dependency* half is implied. Its residue is a **naming** rule: it
 11034	    70	   rejects any `verter_*` token on a non-comment line in `crates/verter_audit/src`, including
 11035	    71	   ones that are not dependencies at all — that is exactly what it caught during A4, when the
 11036	    72	   scope macro's local binding `_verter_attribution_scope` tripped it. A closure walk cannot see
 11037	    73	   a local variable name. So `B1` decides explicitly: either the naming rule is worth keeping as
 11038	    74	   a separate, named, grandfathered guard, or it is dropped as coverage the program does not
 11039	    75	   need. Silently deleting it and calling the closure test a superset would lose real coverage.
 11040	    76	
 11041	    77	## 3. A5's proposed layer assignment
 11042	    78	
 11043	    79	ADR-015's chain, resolved to this workspace's crates. **`B1` ratifies this; A5 proposes it and
 11044	    80	supplies the evidence.**
 11045	    81	
 11046	    82	| layer | ADR-015 name | crates |
 11047	    83	|---|---|---|
 11048	    84	| 1 | identity / span / language / contracts | `verter_span`, `verter_language`, `verter_ecma`, `verter_analysis_inputs`, `verter_audit`, `verter_no_typeexpr`(+`_derive`), `verter_no_storedspan`(+`_derive`) |
 11049	    85	| 2 | shared syntax frontends + dependency-neutral DTOs | `verter_type_expr`, `verter_type_expr_oxc`, `verter_parser`, `verter_css_syntax`, `verter_macro_dto`, `verter_session_query` |
 11050	    86	| 3 | semantic kernel / module resolver / relation / flow | `verter_semantic`, `verter_diagnostics`, `verter_actions` |
 11051	    87	| 4 | compiler | `verter_compiler` |
 11052	    88	| 5 | managed engine / session | `verter_session`, `verter_workspace`, `verter_scheduler`, `verter_tsgo_api`, `verter_type_runtime`, `verter_protocol` |
 11053	    89	| 6 | adapters | `verter_lsp`, `verter_napi`, `verter_wasm`, `verter_ffi`, `verter_mcp`, `verter_mcp_server`, `verter_tsc`, `verter_relay_shim`, `verter-editor-client` |
 11054	    90	| 7 | harnesses (outside ADR-015; no crate may depend on these) | `verter_bench`, `verter_dx_baseline`, `verter_vue_conformance`, `verter_svelte_conformance`, `verter_session_oracle_macro` |
 11055	    91	
 11056	    92	Two placements need justification because they are the ones a reviewer will challenge:
 11057	    93	
 11058	    94	- **`verter_protocol` at layer 5, not layer 2.** ADR-015's layer 2 is *dependency-neutral* DTOs.
 11059	    95	  `verter_protocol` depends on `verter_semantic` (7 references, all
 11060	    96	  `analysis::component_meta::OrderedSfcStructureAnalysis` plus `refs`), so it is not neutral. It
 11061	    97	  is a transport projection above the kernel. `verter_macro_dto` is the crate that actually
 11062	    98	  satisfies layer 2's neutrality, and its closure guard proves it.
 11063	    99	- **`verter_audit` at layer 1.** Its production closure is exactly
 11064	   100	  `{verter_audit, verter_span}` — verified by closure walk. It is a leaf by construction.
 11065	   101	
 11066	   102	## 4. The two upward edges in the current tree
 11067	   103	
 11068	   104	Running the proposed matrix over the resolved graph yields **exactly two** production edges that
 11069	   105	point upward:
 11070	   106	
 11071	   107	```text
 11072	   108	L3 verter_semantic     ->  L5 verter_workspace   (normal)
 11073	   109	L3 verter_diagnostics  ->  L5 verter_workspace   (normal)
 11074	   110	```
 11075	   111	
 11076	   112	`verter_semantic` uses `verter_workspace::WorkspaceRead` (6 sites), `resolver`, `types`,
 11077	   113	`fact_registry`, and `FilesystemWorkspace`.
 11078	   114	
 11079	   115	**This is not repairable by re-layering.** The tempting fix — move `verter_workspace` down to
 11080	   116	layer 2 — fails, because `verter_workspace` itself depends on `verter_scheduler` and
 11081	   117	`verter_tsgo_api`. The two are declared differently, and `B1` must not conflate them
 11082	   118	(`crates/verter_workspace/Cargo.toml`):
 11083	   119	
 11084	   120	| dep | declaration | reach |
 11085	   121	|---|---|---|
 11086	   122	| `verter_scheduler` | `[dependencies]`, line 37 | unconditional — every target |
 11087	   123	| `verter_tsgo_api` | `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]`, line 49 | native only; absent from a `wasm32` build |
 11088	   124	
 11089	   125	So the edge is real on every target, and its consequence is measurable — but the `verter_tsgo_api`
 11090	   126	half of that consequence is **native-only**:
 11091	   127	
 11092	   128	```text
 11093	   129	verter_semantic's production closure (--all-features, normal+build, transitive):
 11094	   130	  verter_audit  verter_css_syntax  verter_ecma  verter_language
 11095	   131	  verter_no_storedspan(+_derive)  verter_no_typeexpr(+_derive)  verter_parser
 11096	   132	  verter_scheduler  verter_span  verter_tsgo_api  verter_type_expr
 11097	   133	  verter_type_expr_oxc  verter_workspace
 11098	   134	```
 11099	   135	
 11100	   136	That closure is the `--all-features` **native** resolve, which is what `cargo metadata` reports by
 11101	   137	default and what the closure test will read.
 11102	   138	
 11103	   139	**The semantic kernel's production closure reaches the task scheduler unconditionally, and the
 11104	   140	external tsgo API on native targets.** ADR-015's stated consequence — "semantic kernel remains
 11105	   141	reusable across lifecycles" — does not hold today: linking the kernel links a task scheduler on
 11106	   142	every target, and additionally an out-of-process tool client on everything but `wasm32`. The
 11107	   143	platform split narrows the second half of the violation; it does not repair either half, because a
 11108	   144	`wasm32`-only firewall is not a firewall.
 11109	   145	
 11110	   146	Compare the crates that *do* satisfy their firewall:
 11111	   147	
 11112	   148	```text
 11113	   149	verter_audit      -> verter_audit  verter_span
 11114	   150	verter_macro_dto  -> verter_macro_dto  verter_no_storedspan(+_derive)  verter_no_typeexpr(+_derive)  verter_span
 11115	   151	```
 11116	   152	
 11117	   153	Reproduce all three with the closure walk over `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features`,
 11118	   154	following `resolve.nodes[].deps` and skipping deps whose `dep_kinds` are all `dev`.
 11119	   155	
 11120	   156	### Disposition
 11121	   157	
 11122	   158	```text
 11123	   159	DEBT A5-DD1  Disposition: DEFER
 11124	   160	  Finding:          verter_semantic (and verter_diagnostics) depend on verter_workspace, so the
 11125	   161	                    semantic kernel's production closure reaches verter_scheduler (unconditional)
 11126	   162	                    and verter_tsgo_api (native only — declared under
 11127	   163	                    cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32")) in verter_workspace/Cargo.toml),
 11128	   164	                    contradicting ADR-015's reusability consequence
 11129	   165	  Durable owner:    C1 (converge ModuleResolverCore / non-flow TypeInfoCore — the block that
 11130	   166	                    decides what the kernel's input surface is), with B1 owning the test that
 11131	   167	                    makes the violation fail rather than be reviewed for
 11132	   168	  Resolution gate:  C1 accepted candidate. B1 MAY land its test with this pair as a recorded,
 11133	   169	                    equality-pinned exception; it MUST NOT land it as a subset-checked allowance,
 11134	   170	                    and the exception must name C1 as its removal gate.
 11135	   171	  Acceptance:       verter_semantic's closure contains neither verter_scheduler nor
 11136	   172	                    verter_tsgo_api on ANY target; the closure test fails if either returns.
 11137	   173	                    B1's equality-pinned exception must therefore record the target condition
 11138	   174	                    alongside the edge, so a wasm32-only resolve cannot read as satisfied.
 11139	   175	  Ruling reference: PENDING
 11140	   176	```
 11141	   177	
 11142	   178	The `B1`-may-land-with-exception clause matters: without it, `B1` either cannot land its own exit
 11143	   179	criterion or is tempted to weaken the test to green. The equality pin plus a named removal gate is
 11144	   180	what keeps a temporary exception from becoming permanent.
 11145	   181	
 11146	   182	## 5. What the strategy deliberately does not cover
 11147	   183	
 11148	   184	- **Intra-crate direction.** The closure walk sees crates. `verter_session` is 5 of the 6 layers
 11149	   185	  by volume, and the module-level direction inside it is not testable this way. ADR-015 is
 11150	   186	  explicit that "logical owners do not automatically require crates; use modules/functions until
 11151	   187	  a real dependency firewall … exists" — so intra-crate direction is held by the type system
 11152	   188	  (privacy, sealed traits, the `NoTypeExpr` marker) and by review, not by this test. `K3` is the
 11153	   189	  block that turns the module boundaries that matter into crate boundaries.
 11154	   190	- **Trait-object back-edges.** A closure walk cannot see a callback that inverts control without
 11155	   191	  inverting the dependency. ADR-015 rejects "mutual compiler/semantic callbacks" for this reason;
 11156	   192	  detecting them is a review mandate, not a graph query.

 12336	     2

 12340	     6	C1 converges the current host-backed module/type-resolution stack — `verter_session::resolver_core`,
 12341	     7	`verter_session::resolver_store`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, and the TypeScript-style resolver living in
 12342	     8	`verter_workspace::resolver` — into the two target logical owners named in `architecture.md` §8.1: a
 12343	     9	`ModuleResolverCore` that owns TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution, and a non-flow
 12344	    10	`TypeInfoCore` that owns authored-node traversal, binder/name/reference semantics, substitution,
 12345	    11	relation/inference, effective typing, recursion/work budgets, query-specific projection, and
 12346	    12	exactness/completeness propagation. Neither target type exists in code today; both names describe roles
 12347	    13	the current tree already plays under different names and in the wrong crate. C1 does not invent new
 12348	    14	resolution semantics — every module/name/type/relation answer the converged kernel gives must be
 12349	    15	identical to today's answer for every existing lifecycle. It changes who owns the code, how many
 12350	    16	duplicate implementations of the same lifecycle-adapter shape exist, whether the kernel can perform I/O
 12351	    17	directly, and where the crate boundary sits.
 12352	    18	
 12353	    19	C1 does not own flow semantics (`D1`–`D8`), Vue/Svelte macro projection (`C3`), the staged
 12354	    20	prepare/plan/project/emit compile transaction or its anti-replay tokens (`C2`), or component-meta
 12355	    21	publication policy (`/component-meta`). It extends nothing about `execute_relate`'s relation semantics or
 12356	    22	`ProjectSemanticDispatch`'s five query modes — those are `Preserve`, not `Converge`, dispositions. It owns
 12357	    23	convergence of context/lifecycle plumbing, dependency direction, and the addition of a batched,
 12358	    24	resumable load-outcome so a future I/O-free lifecycle can consume the same kernel a blocking lifecycle
 12359	    25	consumes today.
 12360	    26	
 12361	    27	## Intent Contract
 12362	    28	
 12363	    29	**Actor / problem.** Every current and future first-party consumer of Verter's type/module resolution —
 12364	    30	the host-backed LSP session, the session-overlay (unsaved-edit) path, and the future project-aware direct
 12365	    31	compiler (`C2`'s sealed `CompileTypeInfo`) — must resolve a symbol, import, or type to the *same* answer.
 12366	    32	Today that guarantee is held by convention (three lifecycle adapters hand-implement the same sealed
 12367	    33	`ResolverContext` trait with large amounts of copy-pasted delegation) and by omission (no lifecycle exists
 12368	    34	yet that cannot block a thread on I/O), not by a structural authority that forces convergence and permits
 12369	    35	a new I/O-free lifecycle to be added without duplicating resolution logic a fourth time.
 12370	    36	
 12371	    37	**Required observable outcomes.**
 12372	    38	- A module/name/type/relation query issued through `HostResolverContext`, `SessionResolverContext`, or
 12373	    39	  (once added) an I/O-free project-capable context returns bit-identical `SemanticNodeId`/resolved-surface
 12374	    40	  results for the same source content, project configuration, and query, modulo the outcome shape
 12375	    41	  (blocking-complete vs. `NeedInputs`).
 12376	    42	- A resolver-tier operation that needs a not-yet-loaded dependency and runs under an I/O-free environment
 12377	    43	  returns `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` (per `contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4) instead of
 12378	    44	  panicking, blocking, or fabricating a partial answer.
 12379	    45	- `verter_semantic`'s production dependency closure contains neither `verter_scheduler` nor
 12380	    46	  `verter_tsgo_api` on any target (closes debt row A5-DD1, `evidence/A5/dependency-direction.md:158-176`).
 12381	    47	- The sealed `ResolverContext` trait (`resolver_core/resolver_context.rs:161`) has exactly as many
 12382	    48	  production-reachable implementors as there are genuinely distinct lifecycles; a lifecycle that cannot
 12383	    49	  resolve (e.g. a bare host with no request/session binding) is a compile-time impossibility for
 12384	    50	  resolver-tier call sites, not a documented runtime `panic!`.
 12385	    51	
 12386	    52	**Forbidden observable outcomes.**
 12387	    53	- A second implementation of `SemanticQueryApi::execute`, `execute_relate`, `shallow_lower_type_expr`, a
 12388	    54	  second struct owning a `RelationMemo` or the semantic node map (the existing Authority-uniqueness
 12389	    55	  contract, `.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:826-832` — C1 preserves this unchanged).
 12390	    56	- A converged kernel that reads live, un-snapshotted host state at validation time (defeats "immutable
 12391	    57	  observation views").
 12392	    58	- A lifecycle-specific answer: the same query returning a different resolved type, a different route, or
 12393	    59	  a different completeness verdict depending on which `ResolverContext` implementor served it, for
 12394	    60	  identical inputs.
 12395	    61	- A blocking wait introduced on the path a future I/O-free lifecycle uses to reach `NeedInputs` — the
 12396	    62	  point of the new outcome is that that path never calls `wait_or_drive`/`Condvar::wait`.
 12397	    63	
 12398	    64	**Authority/fallback order.** `SemanticQueryKey → ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute → SemanticGraphStore`
 12399	    65	remains the sole query-time resolver (`project_semantic_dispatch/mod.rs:2206-2214`, the shared choke
 12400	    66	point). `ResolverContext` implementors are lifecycle *adapters* over that one authority, never alternate
 12401	    67	authorities. A resolver-tier operation that cannot prove a current, coherent view fails closed to a typed
 12402	    68	non-current miss (`StoreViewRead`'s `CurrentHostStoreView`/`ColdSeedHostStoreView` split,
 12403	    69	`.claude/skills/host-session/SKILL.md:678-696`) — C1 preserves this fail-closed order and must not weaken

 12461	   127	## Batched `NeedInputs` contract
 12462	   128	
 12463	   129	C1 owns the **kernel-level** attempt outcome: a resolver-core operation run under an I/O-free environment
 12464	   130	returns `AttemptOutcome::{Complete(T), NeedInputs(LoadSet), Terminal(AttemptFailure)}` per
 12465	   131	`contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4, instead of calling `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
 12466	   132	synchronously. `LoadSet` is normalized/sorted/deduplicated; `NeedInputs` on an empty delta with no basis
 12467	   133	change is the typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` failure (§4.3-4.5 of that contract), never a silent retry
 12468	   134	loop. This capability does not exist anywhere in the tree today (`grep -rn "NeedInputs\|LoadSet"
 12469	   135	crates/` — zero hits) and is new work, not a refactor of an existing batching mechanism.
 12470	   136	
 12471	   137	**C1 does not own** the outer staged transaction. `contracts/input-loading.md` §5: "A direct/project
 12472	   138	`CompileTypeInfo` over an immutable caller environment does not own commits or I/O. It returns
 12473	   139	`NeedInputs`; the caller may rebuild/extend the environment and retry." That caller — the
 12474	   140	prepare/plan/project/emit loop, `CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, and the
 12475	   141	load/commit/retry orchestration across *multiple* kernel attempts — is `C2` (`program.md:242-247`, ADR-011).
 12476	   142	C1's obligation ends at: one resolver-tier operation, one immutable snapshot, one typed outcome. C2's
 12477	   143	obligation starts at: drive repeated C1 attempts, own the snapshot-extend/retry loop, own the anti-replay
 12478	   144	tokens.
 12479	   145	
 12480	   146	The existing blocking behavior is **not deleted**: the host-backed LSP session and the session-overlay
 12481	   147	lifecycle are permitted, documented lifecycles that legitimately block a cooperating thread
 12482	   148	(`decl_body_memo.rs:21`, `store_view_manager_tests.rs:2399` — "in-flight work block cooperatively, never
 12483	   149	busy-spin"). C1 adds the alternative outcome so a *new* I/O-free lifecycle can reuse the same resolution
 12484	   150	logic without being forced to block; it does not retrofit every existing call site to stop blocking.
 12485	   151

 12521	   187	## Structural confinement
 12522	   188	
 12523	   189	Every invariant above is enforced structurally, matching the pattern the codebase already uses in this
 12524	   190	exact area — C1 extends that pattern, it does not invent scanner-based enforcement:
 12525	   191	
 12526	   192	- **Sealed-trait lifecycle closure.** `ResolverContext: sealed::Sealed` (`resolver_context.rs:82-98,161`)
 12527	   193	  already makes "some fourth, unregistered lifecycle adapter" a compile error. C1 preserves the seal and,
 12528	   194	  if the bare-host rail is deleted (see above), tightens `RequestBoundResolverContext`
 12529	   195	  (`resolver_context.rs:780-815`, `static_assertions::assert_obj_safe!`) from "narrower than
 12530	   196	  `ResolverContext`" to "identical to it" — a resolver-tier function taking `&dyn ResolverContext` becomes
 12531	   197	  provably request-bound by construction, not by convention.
 12532	   198	- **`StoreView`/`HostStoreView` immutability is already structural**, not a convention: `HostStoreView`
 12533	   199	  (`resolver_store.rs:1462-1525`) has no `&VerterHost`/`Arc<Mutex<..>>` field, only `Arc`-shared by-value
 12534	   200	  snapshot data; a future violation (a live host reference smuggled into the struct) is a visible field
 12535	   201	  addition a reviewer catches at the type definition, not a runtime behavior to detect.
 12536	   202	- **The Authority-uniqueness contract** (`.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:826-832`: no second
 12537	   203	  `SemanticQueryApi` impl, no second `execute_relate`, no second `shallow_lower_type_expr`, no second
 12538	   204	  `RelationMemo` owner, no second semantic-node-map owner) is enforced today partly by a `syn`-AST content
 12539	   205	  scanner (`crates/verter_session/tests/cases/architecture_guards.rs:3384` `mod resolver_context_seal`,
 12540	   206	  reached from `no_concrete_verter_host_in_seal_scope` at `:3703-3712`) and partly by grandfathered
 12541	   207	  string-content assertions (e.g. `resolver_store_view_returns_store_view_read` at `:16454-16469`). Per
 12542	   208	  `CLAUDE.md`'s forward-only landed-scanner rule, these are **grandfathered, not a template**: C1 must not
 12543	   209	  add a new name-keyed source scanner for any *new* invariant it introduces (the deleted bare-host rail,
 12544	   210	  the collapsed duplication, the new `AttemptOutcome`). New confinement is type-level: privacy, the
 12545	   211	  existing seal, a marker type for "I/O-free context" analogous to `RequestBoundResolverContext`, or a
 12546	   212	  `NoTypeExpr`-style content-free marker if `AttemptOutcome<T>` needs one. C1 may *extend* the existing
 12547	   213	  grandfathered scanners' checked assertions if a change under review genuinely regresses what they
 12548	   214	  already check; it may not add a new standalone scanner test.
 12549	   215	- **`NeedInputs` non-blocking guarantee.** The cleanest structural proof available is a marker type on the
 12550	   216	  I/O-free context (e.g. an `IoFreeResolverContext` sealed subtrait, mirroring
 12551	   217	  `RequestBoundResolverContext`'s shape) that is never implemented for any type holding a `&VerterHost`
 12552	   218	  capable of reaching the scheduler — so a resolver-tier function generic over that marker cannot call
 12553	   219	  `ensure_loaded` even if someone tries, because the trait bound does not expose it. This is a design
 12554	   220	  recommendation, not a locked mechanism; see Open Questions.

 12556	   222	## Boundary against flow (D-track) and against C2
 12557	   223	
 12558	   224	**Flow exclusion.** C1 converges the relation/inference authority (`execute_relate`,
 12559	   225	`project_semantic_dispatch/relation.rs`) exactly as it stands today — `Preserve`, not `Converge`. It adds
 12560	   226	no flow-specific relation classifier, no binding-slot integration, no nominal-identity/unique-symbol
 12561	   227	comparability extension. Those are `D3`'s stated job: "Extend the already-shared relation authority with
 12562	   228	nominal identities including unique symbols and tri-state comparability" (`program.md:249-253`). C1's only
 12563	   229	obligation to the flow track is that the relation authority it converges remains the single authority `D1`
 12564	   230	integrates against behind its private non-production test boundary (`program.md:229`) and that `D3` later
 12565	   231	extends without needing a second relation/name authority (`program.md:253`: "No flow-private relation/name
 12566	   232	authority may exist after `D2`"). If convergence work touches `project_semantic_dispatch/relation.rs`,
 12567	   233	`relation_txn.rs`, or the `RelationMemo` at all, it is confined to lifecycle/context plumbing around the
 12568	   234	call, never the relation algorithm itself.
 12569	   235	
 12570	   236	**C2 boundary.** C2 owns the staged compile transaction: `prepare → plan → project → emit`,
 12571	   237	`CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, `CompileFactsBatch`, the concrete sealed
 12572	   238	`CompileTypeInfo`, and the outer load/commit/retry loop over C1's `NeedInputs` outcome (ADR-011,
 12573	   239	`program.md:242-247`). C1 must not build any of that — no plan token, no fact batch, no staged
 12574	   240	prepare/plan/project/emit state machine. C1's deliverable to C2 is: a `ResolverContext`-shaped kernel
 12575	   241	(or its post-extraction equivalent) that (a) gives identical answers across lifecycles, (b) can be driven
 12576	   242	from an I/O-free environment and returns `NeedInputs` instead of blocking, and (c) can be constructed
 12577	   243	without pulling in `verter_scheduler`/`verter_tsgo_api`/LSP-facing machinery, so C2's compiler-facing
 12578	   244	facade does not have to depend on the whole `verter_session` crate to embed it.
 12579	   245	
 12580	   246	## Required exit
 12581	   247	
 12582	   248	Per `program.md:196`: **lifecycle differs; module/name/type/relation meaning does not.** Concretely: the
 12583	   249	three (or more, once the I/O-free context exists) `ResolverContext` implementors give bit-identical
 12584	   250	resolved answers for identical inputs; the duplicated boilerplate between `HostResolverContext` and
 12585	   251	`SessionResolverContext` is gone; `verter_semantic`'s production closure excludes `verter_scheduler` and
 12586	   252	`verter_tsgo_api` on every target with no exception recorded; `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` exists
 12587	   253	and is exercised by at least one real resolver-tier load point without touching the scheduler; the
 12588	   254	Authority-uniqueness contract's five rows still hold; no `TypeExpr`-general transit, flow semantics, or
 12589	   255	C2-owned staged-transaction machinery was introduced.

 12612	   277	## Open questions requiring maintainer/architecture ruling
 12613	   278	
 12614	   279	These are gaps this research could not close from the code and evidence tree alone. Do not dispatch
 12615	   280	implementation against them without a ruling — each is a real design fork, not a detail:
 12616	   281	
 12617	   282	1. **Crate placement.** `resolver_core`/`resolver_store` are today private modules inside `verter_session`
 12618	   283	   with no crate boundary between them (confirmed: `lib.rs:341-344`, plain `use crate::resolver_store::…`
 12619	   284	   intra-crate references throughout). `architecture.md` §18.1 places "semantic kernel/module
 12620	   285	   resolver/relation/flow" *below* "compiler" and far below "managed engine/session" in the inward
 12621	   286	   dependency chain, which today's placement inverts. Whether C1 must physically extract the converged
 12622	   287	   kernel into a new crate (and if so, its name, its exact member boundary, and whether extraction happens
 12623	   288	   inside C1 or is staged into a follow-up block C1 merely proves is possible) is the single largest open
 12624	   289	   design question in this charter. I did not find an existing target crate name or extraction plan in
 12625	   290	   `architecture.md`, the ADRs, or `program-dag.toml` — this needs an explicit pre-implementation
 12626	   291	   architecture challenge (governance.md's Foundational-class requirement), not a decision made inside
 12627	   292	   the charter.
 12628	   293	2. **A5-DD1's harder half.** `verter_semantic/src/analysis/routes.rs`'s `&dyn verter_workspace::WorkspaceRead`
 12629	   294	   parameter (6 call sites) is a genuine functional dependency, not a re-export. Closing the
 12630	   295	   `verter_semantic → verter_workspace` edge requires either relocating `WorkspaceRead` to a lower neutral
 12631	   296	   layer or moving route-extraction logic upward to where `WorkspaceRead` already lives — I could not
 12632	   297	   determine from the code which is correct without risking a guess that contradicts `F1`'s
 12633	   298	   not-yet-written committed-input-authority design. Flagged, not resolved, in Legacy Deletions above.
 12634	   299	3. **Whether `NeedInputs` needs a structural (marker-type) non-blocking guarantee or an accepted
 12635	   300	   review-enforced one.** I recommend a sealed `IoFreeResolverContext`-shaped marker (mirroring
 12636	   301	   `RequestBoundResolverContext`) so a resolver-tier function generic over it cannot reach
 12637	   302	   `ensure_loaded`/the scheduler even by accident, but this is materially more invasive than a
 12638	   303	   review-enforced convention and its cost/benefit was not evaluated against a real implementation attempt.
 12639	   304	   This should be settled at the same pre-implementation architecture challenge as (1), since the answer
 12640	   305	   likely depends on it (a marker type is far cheaper to add correctly if the extraction in (1) happens
 12641	   306	   first, because the I/O-free context would then live outside `verter_session` entirely and could not
 12642	   307	   physically hold a `&VerterHost`).
 12643	   308	4. **Scope of "AttemptOutcome" coverage.** `program.md:196` says "return batched `NeedInputs`" without
 12644	   309	   qualifying which resolver-tier operations. This charter scopes it to the load points already reached
 12645	   310	   through `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` (the only synchronous-blocking-on-I/O sites this
 12646	   311	   research found). Whether C2 needs *every* resolver-core query to support the outcome on day one, or
 12647	   312	   whether a narrower first cut (module/import resolution only, deferring full type-query coverage) is
 12648	   313	   acceptable, is a scope call for whoever authors C1's pre-implementation brief — I have not sized the
 12649	   314	   full-coverage option against the fan-out of `resolver_core`'s ~37 files.
