 13209	     1	# Snapshot-Consistent Batched Input Loading Contract
 13210	     2	
 13211	     3	**Status:** Normative outer-orchestration contract.
 13212	     4	
 13213	     5	# 1. Kernel rule
 13214	     6	
 13215	     7	The compiler, resolver, TypeInfo, flow, and reusable query kernels consume one immutable observation view per attempt and perform no hidden filesystem/network/process/package-manager I/O.
 13216	     8	
 13217	     9	# 2. Outcome
 13218	    10	
 13219	    11	```rust
 13220	    12	enum AttemptOutcome<T> {
 13221	    13	    Complete(T),
 13222	    14	    NeedInputs(LoadSet),
 13223	    15	    Terminal(AttemptFailure),
 13224	    16	}
 13225	    17	```
 13226	    18	
 13227	    19	`LoadSet` is normalized, sorted, deduplicated, and includes the resolution basis needed to load/commit safely. The kernel discovers all independently reachable missing observations it can identify without fabricating semantic answers.
 13228	    20	
 13229	    21	# 3. Orchestration state
 13230	    22	
 13231	    23	```text
 13232	    24	attempt number
 13233	    25	current snapshot identity
 13234	    26	accumulated requested InputKeys
 13235	    27	accumulated stable positive/negative observations
 13236	    28	unique input count
 13237	    29	loaded byte count
 13238	    30	dependency depth/frontier
 13239	    31	basis-change/churn count
 13240	    32	```
 13241	    33	
 13242	    34	# 4. Algorithm
 13243	    35	
 13244	    36	1. Run the whole operation against snapshot `S`.
 13245	    37	2. On `Complete`, validate observed facts against `S` and return/admit according to the query contract.
 13246	    38	3. On `Terminal`, return typed failure and never admit complete state.
 13247	    39	4. On `NeedInputs(L)`, normalize `L` and calculate `delta = L.keys - accumulated_requested`.
 13248	    40	5. If `delta` is empty and neither the resolution basis nor any previously observed fact changed, return `InputResolutionNoProgress` with the unresolved set.
 13249	    41	6. Check configured limits before I/O: attempts, unique keys, bytes, dependency depth, and basis-change/churn count.
 13250	    42	7. Load `delta` through embedding-owned same-key I/O flights. Each result is `Present`, stable `Missing`, or transient `LoadFailure`, with typed metadata and basis. Public/external loader digests are hints: the committing authority verifies key/basis consistency and computes or verifies content/configuration fingerprints from captured data before publication.
 13251	    43	8. Conditionally publish all validated commit-eligible observations as one coherent input batch only if the project/configuration basis remains compatible.
 13252	    44	9. If conditional commit loses a race or the basis changed, capture the new coherent snapshot, increment churn budget, and restart. Do not splice data into the old attempt.
 13253	    45	10. If committed, capture the new snapshot and restart from step 1.
 13254	    46	
 13255	    47	# 5. Direct project mode
 13256	    48	
 13257	    49	A direct/project `CompileTypeInfo` over an immutable caller environment does not own commits or I/O. It returns `NeedInputs`; the caller may rebuild/extend the environment and retry. The same no-progress/resource rules apply to convenience orchestration APIs.
 13258	    50	
 13259	    51	# 6. Observation trust boundary
 13260	    52	
 13261	    53	- public environments/loaders cannot mint authoritative `ContentId`, `InputBasisId`, semantic read facts, or completeness evidence;
 13262	    54	- source bytes, declared language/source type, canonical source identity, package/config metadata, lengths, and supplied digests are consistency-checked at capture/commit;
 13263	    55	- the authoritative owner hashes/normalizes once per committed revision and reuses the typed IDs thereafter;
 13264	    56	- a sealed first-party `EngineSnapshot` may carry prevalidated IDs because the same authority minted them;
 13265	    57	- mismatched key/bytes/profile/basis is a typed integrity failure and is never cached as stable missing or complete.
 13266	    58	
 13267	    59	# 7. Negative facts
 13268	    60	
 13269	    61	A stable missing module/package/file may be observed and cached only with the complete resolution basis: parent/package boundaries, conditions, path/case/symlink/workspace policy, and relevant configuration. Transient permission/network/process/provider failure is not a stable negative semantic fact.
 13270	    62	
 13271	    63	# 8. Resource failures
 13272	    64	
 13273	    65	Distinct failures include:
 13274	    66	
 13275	    67	```text
 13276	    68	InputResolutionNoProgress
 13277	    69	InputResolutionAttemptLimit
 13278	    70	InputResolutionUniqueKeyLimit
 13279	    71	InputResolutionByteLimit
 13280	    72	InputResolutionDepthLimit
 13281	    73	InputResolutionChurnLimit
 13282	    74	InputLoadUnavailable
 13283	    75	InputCommitConflictExceeded
 13284	    76	```
 13285	    77	
 13286	    78	They carry unresolved keys and consumed budget without exposing sensitive ambient paths beyond the product's diagnostic policy.
 13287	    79	
 13288	    80	# 9. Tests
 13289	    81	
 13290	    82	- multiple missing siblings loaded in one batch;
 13291	    83	- transitive dependency waves;
 13292	    84	- stable missing negative fact;
 13293	    85	- dependency appears between attempts;
 13294	    86	- project/config changes during load;
 13295	    87	- repeated same `LoadSet` no progress;
 13296	    88	- loader partial/transient failure;
 13297	    89	- unique key/byte/depth/retry/churn limits;
 13298	    90	- external observation digest/key mismatch rejected before commit;
 13299	    91	- no semantic kernel I/O instrumentation;
 13300	    92	- final result equals an equivalent fully preloaded clean run.
 13301	     1	# Staged Compile Transaction and Anti-Replay Contract
 13302	     2	
 13303	     3	**Status:** Normative direct/prepared/project-aware compiler protocol.
 13304	     4	
 13305	     5	# 1. Stages
 13306	     6	
 13307	     7	```text
 13308	     8	prepare(source, parse options)
 13309	     9	  -> PreparedCarrier
 13310	    10	plan(prepared, CompileRequest)
 13311	    11	  -> CompilePlan
 13312	    12	project(plan.projection_batch, CompileTypeInfo)
 13313	    13	  -> CompleteFacts | NeedInputs(LoadSet) | TerminalFailure
 13314	    14	emit(prepared, plan, complete facts)
 13315	    15	  -> CompileResult
 13316	    16	```
 13317	    17	
 13318	    18	Planning discovers the complete product prerequisite closure and closed semantic projection batch before projection. Emission does not discover new project-semantic demands. A new demand requires a new plan.
 13319	    19	
 13320	    20	# 2. Binding tokens
 13321	    21	
 13322	    22	`CompilePlanToken` binds the complete request for anti-replay. The plan additionally owns narrower deterministic tokens:
 13323	    23	
 13324	    24	```text
 13325	    25	ProjectionPlanToken   root + semantic profile + closed demand batch + kernel/projection domains
 13326	    26	ProductSubplanToken   root + framework/product + output profile + required product mapping contract
 13327	    27	TerminalSubplanToken  exact typed result/product + requested presentation/provenance/encoding profile
 13328	    28	```
 13329	    29	
 13330	    30	The whole `CompilePlanToken` binds at least:
 13331	    31	
 13332	    32	- prepared root/source/unit identities;
 13333	    33	- parse key/domain and relevant generation;
 13334	    34	- normalized canonical typed product-request collection;
 13335	    35	- shared semantic profile when observed;
 13336	    36	- each product's output and requested terminal presentation/mapping/provenance/serialization profiles;
 13337	    37	- framework/compiler compatibility identity;
 13338	    38	- projection schema/domain;
 13339	    39	- plan algorithm compatibility domain;
 13340	    40	- deterministic demand ordering and digest.
 13341	    41	
 13342	    42	The plan contains independently keyed subplans/artifact identities. A presentation-, map-encoding-, provenance-, or serialization-only change may create a new terminal subplan without invalidating an unchanged semantic projection or code-generation subplan. `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete request for anti-replay; it does not force every subartifact to use that whole token as its cache key.
 13343	    43	
 13344	    44	`CompileFactsBatch` binds:
 13345	    45	
 13346	    46	- exact `ProjectionPlanToken` and demand digest referenced by the containing plan;
 13347	    47	- semantic profile and kernel compatibility domain;
 13348	    48	- input basis and observed dependency fingerprints;
 13349	    49	- one typed result for every demand;
 13350	    50	- exactness/completeness/degradation;
 13351	    51	- integrity and size limits when decoded or transferred.
 13352	    52	
 13353	    53	Emission first validates the whole `CompilePlanToken`, then validates that the facts satisfy the exact `ProjectionPlanToken` referenced by that plan. It rejects missing, extra, duplicated, reordered without canonical identity, stale, wrong-profile, wrong-projection-plan, wrong-root, wrong-domain, or insufficient facts before output construction.
 13354	    54	
 13355	    55	# 3. Zero-demand behavior
 13356	    56	
 13357	    57	When the plan has no semantic projection demands:
 13358	    58	
 13359	    59	- no `CompileTypeInfo` session is constructed;
 13360	    60	- no module resolver or TypeInfo index/graph/flow work runs;
 13361	    61	- projection stage is represented as an empty complete batch bound to the plan;
 13362	    62	- Svelte current runtime compilation must prove zero Vue/native projection demand unless its capability contract changes.
 13363	    63	
 13364	    64	# 4. `NeedInputs`
 13365	    65	
 13366	    66	`NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a resumable orchestration outcome. It does not mutate the current plan or prepared value with unversioned ambient data. The outer orchestrator loads and publishes/rebuilds a coherent input view according to `input-loading.md`, then reruns projection with the same plan only when the plan’s source/request/profile basis remains valid. Otherwise it replans.
 13367	    67	
 13368	    68	# 5. Direct and managed modes
 13369	    69	
 13370	    70	- local direct mode may project from the retained root only;
 13371	    71	- direct project mode consumes an immutable caller-provided observation view and returns `NeedInputs` to the caller;
 13372	    72	- managed mode consumes one `EngineSnapshot`/`InputBasisId` per attempt and uses the outer commit/retry loop;
 13373	    73	- all modes execute one semantic kernel and the same closed framework projector;
 13374	    74	- lifecycle, retention, and orchestration differ; semantics do not.
 13375	    75	
 13376	    76	# 6. Error taxonomy
 13377	    77	
 13378	    78	Distinct failures include parse/preparation failure, unsupported product combination, unavailable semantic capability, `NeedInputs`, no progress, projection gap, unresolved dependency, stale plan/facts, profile/domain mismatch, size/integrity failure, cancellation, budget exhaustion, and internal failure.
 13379	    79	
 13380	    80	# 7. Required tests
 13381	    81	
 13382	    82	- plan once and emit multiple requested products without rediscovery;
 13383	    83	- simultaneous product combinations equal separately requested products where contracts declare composability;
 13384	    84	- different per-product output profiles coexist without a global-profile collision;
 13385	    85	- presentation/serialization-only changes reuse unchanged semantic and code subplans;
 13386	    86	- irrelevant product/profile fields are rejected or normalized away before identity construction;
 13387	    87	- zero-demand zero-initialization;
 13388	    88	- local and imported projection batches;
 13389	    89	- batched shared-root deduplication;
 13390	    90	- stale/wrong-whole-plan/wrong-projection-plan/wrong-profile/extra/missing facts rejected;
 13391	    91	- facts from a terminal-only sibling plan are accepted only when their `ProjectionPlanToken` is exactly equal;
 13392	    92	- `NeedInputs` waves and no-progress behavior;
 13393	    93	- basis change forces retry/replan as appropriate;
 13394	    94	- direct/prepared/managed output equality for equal product/profile/input contracts;
 13395	    95	- cancelled/superseded attempts do not terminally materialize output.

 13417	     1	# ADR-003 — Compile Semantics Use a Concrete Sealed Facade
 13418	     2	
 13419	     3	**Status:** Accepted
 13420	     4	
 13421	     5	## Context
 13422	     6	
 13423	     7	The compiler needs optional project-aware semantic projections. An open trait would permit alternate module/type/runtime-classification semantics and create a second engine.
 13424	     8	
 13425	     9	## Decision
 13426	    10	
 13427	    11	The compiler accepts only a concrete Verter-owned `CompileTypeInfo<'_>` facade. Lifecycle variants are private/sealed first-party constructions. External integrations may supply captured observations through a data-only environment; they cannot implement semantic behavior.
 13428	    12	
 13429	    13	All construction modes execute one profile-parameterized semantic kernel and one module resolver. The facade has no blanket `Send + Sync`; ownership/concurrency is a lifecycle policy.
 13430	    14	
 13431	    15	## Consequences
 13432	    16	
 13433	    17	Direct local, captured-project, in-memory, engine-snapshot, and validated-precomputed modes remain possible without opening semantics or coupling the compiler to `Engine`.
 13434	    18	
 13435	    19	## Rejected alternatives
 13436	    20	
 13437	    21	- public semantic trait object;
 13438	    22	- compiler receives host/Engine/provider state;
 13439	    23	- framework/compiler-local resolver fallback.
 13440	     1	# ADR-011 — Project-Aware Compile Uses a Resumable I/O-Free Transaction
 13441	     2	
 13442	     3	**Status:** Accepted  
 13443	     4	**Decision owner:** direct compiler/project TypeInfo integration  
 13444	     5	**Reopen only if:** a future compiler mode explicitly embeds I/O and accepts a separate architecture boundary.
 13445	     6	
 13446	     7	## Context
 13447	     8	
 13448	     9	A compile API that may need project inputs cannot safely hide I/O or retain OXC borrows across asynchronous loading. Projection facts must be proven to belong to the exact plan that consumes them.
 13449	    10	
 13450	    11	## Decision
 13451	    12	
 13452	    13	Project-aware compile follows:
 13453	    14	
 13454	    15	```text
 13455	    16	prepare -> plan -> project -> emit
 13456	    17	```
 13457	    18	
 13458	    19	- prepared syntax remains owned/borrowed by one retained owner;
 13459	    20	- the projection batch is compact, owned, and OXC-free;
 13460	    21	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized request to the prepared root; the plan contains narrower deterministic projection/product/terminal subplan tokens;
 13461	    22	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds to the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`, semantic profile, dependency/input basis, projection schema, and demand digest, so terminal-only sibling plans may reuse facts only when that projection token is exactly equal;
 13462	    23	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a first-class resumable outcome;
 13463	    24	- external loading occurs outside compiler/semantic compute;
 13464	    25	- no syntax borrow or unvalidated locator crosses the loading boundary;
 13465	    26	- each attempt reports the maximal sound missing observation set discovered;
 13466	    27	- retries use a monotonic progress ledger, bounded waves/resources, and deterministic no-progress failure;
 13467	    28	- stale or replayed facts are rejected before emission.
 13468	    29	
 13469	    30	## Consequences
 13470	    31	
 13471	    32	The same semantic kernel supports local, captured-project, in-memory, and managed-snapshot modes without hidden filesystem authority.
 13472	    33	
 13473	    34	## Rejected alternatives
 13474	    35	
 13475	    36	- **Synchronous hidden filesystem callbacks:** break hermeticity and coherent snapshots.
 13476	    37	- **Reparse/replan implicitly after every missing input:** can amplify work and consume mismatched facts.
 13477	     1	# ADR-015 — Core Dependency Direction Is Inward and Cycle-Free
 13478	     2	
 13479	     3	**Status:** Accepted  
 13480	     4	**Decision owner:** crate/module ownership  
 13481	     5	**Reopen only if:** a new stable boundary cannot be represented without a cycle and an alternative decomposition has been disproven.
 13482	     6	
 13483	     7	## Context
 13484	     8	
 13485	     9	Where `CompileTypeInfo`, framework projection DTOs, and request contracts live can accidentally create compiler↔semantic or compiler↔session cycles, forcing traits, erasure, and shared ownership.
 13486	    10	
 13487	    11	## Decision
 13488	    12	
 13489	    13	Binding direction is:
 13490	    14	
 13491	    15	```text
 13492	    16	identity/span/language/contracts

 13522	     1	# ADR-001 — One Semantic Authority, Justified Derived Projections
 13523	     2	
 13524	     3	**Status:** Accepted  
 13525	     4	**Decision owner:** TypeInfo/effective-flow architecture
 13526	     5	
 13527	     6	## Context
 13528	     7	
 13529	     8	`FunctionFlowGraph` must be the one structural flow authority, but efficient solving may need dominators, loop forests, SCCs, def-use overlays, capture summaries, reverse adjacency, or compact execution schedules. Forbidding every graph-derived structure would either bloat the canonical graph or repeat topology work. Allowing independent query-specific CFGs recreates the current dual-authority defect.
 13530	     9	
 13531	    10	## Decision
 13532	    11	
 13533	    12	`FunctionFlowGraph` is the canonical structural authority. A derived structure is allowed only when it:
 13534	    13	
 13535	    14	- is keyed by one exact graph/body identity and any interpretation-affecting semantic profile;
 13536	    15	- is deterministic and fully reproducible from the graph and accepted kernel rules;
 13537	    16	- cannot add facts, define transfer/join semantics, mark coverage complete, or publish a semantic result;
 13538	    17	- is request-local by default and independently weighted/evicted if retention is proven valuable;
 13539	    18	- can be replaced without changing observable semantics.
 13540	    19	
 13541	    20	## Consequences
 13542	    21	
 13543	    22	The solver may use efficient layouts without creating a second semantic or control authority. Review checks authority and construction rights, not superficial data-structure count.
 13544	    23	
 13545	    24	## Rejected alternatives
 13546	    25	
 13547	    26	- exactly one physical graph-like object;
 13548	    27	- independent syntax-shaped/query-specific CFGs;
 13549	    28	- projections that own relation, completion, capture, or coverage decisions.

 13757	   475	### Verification Must Prove Execution (MANDATORY)
 13758	   476	
 13759	   477	A required gate passes only on fresh, input-bound evidence that: every applicable required job was eligible and ran; the intended tree-derived surface was owned and independently discovered; selectors matched non-zero work; required source, build, and fixture prerequisites matched the tested tree; executed work was non-zero; unexpected prerequisite skips were zero; child deadlines were strictly below their parent killer; and a terminal summary completed. **Exit status 0 alone, a self-declared test universe, or a missing required-job result is FAIL.** Every tracked test or guard has exactly one declared primary gate; a hand-maintained filename list may not define the primary universe unless generated from independent discovery and parity-checked.
 13760	   478	
 13761	   479	Attestation alone is insufficient — a receipt faithfully attests whatever incomplete universe the runner defines for itself. The durable design needs all three: fresh execution attestation; independently tree-derived inventory/discovery parity; and per-surface negative-control mutation through the exact canonical entry point.     16	## GAP 1 — Cross-crate trait sealing
    17	
    18	Use the repository’s existing idiom exactly:
    19

    24	}
    25

    27	    fn lookup(&self, key: &ObservationKey) -> ObservationValueRef<'_>;

    29

Only code inside `verter_semantic` can name `sealed::Sealed`; a foreign `impl ObservationRead for CompileTypeInfo` fails because `CompileTypeInfo: sealed::Sealed` cannot be satisfied, and attempting the marker impl fails with private-module error E0603. This is the same shape used by:
    35	
    36	- `ResolverContext`: private marker at `crates/verter_session/src/resolver_core/resolver_context.rs:82`, supertrait at `:161`, sanctioned marker impls at `:745`.

They construct it through a semantic-owned builder from immutable data. No callbacks, closures, host references, or trait objects belong in the snapshot.

    43	`CompileTypeInfo` must compose an `ObservationSnapshot` and call the kernel. If it genuinely must implement the interface, the interface cannot remain sealed: Rust has no friend-crate exception. The same applies to external test doubles.     96	## GAP 3 — Full-coverage `AttemptOutcome` proof
    97	
    98	The charter’s exhaustive-`impl` mechanism is invalid.
    99	
   100	- Adding a required method makes an existing impl incomplete, but adding a defaulted method does not. The repo demonstrates this directly: `ResolverContext::is_request_bound` has a default at `resolver_context.rs:179-181`, while the large `impl ResolverContext for VerterHost` beginning at `:817` omits it and compiles.
   101	- Even a required method proves only that the double supplies a body. A new method returning bare `T` can be added, implemented with bare `T`, and the exhaustive impl compiles. The impl does not constrain the trait author’s return type.
   102	- Generic methods, associated output types, and `async fn` do not improve this. They may make the trait non-dyn-compatible—the current code separately pins that at `resolver_context.rs:805-815`—but they do not force `AttemptOutcome`. An associated type can resolve to any type.
   103	- A Rust type alias to `AttemptOutcome<T>` is type-identical and therefore valid. It only defeats textual/name-based checking, not Rust type equality.
   104	- A foreign exhaustive double is forbidden by GAP 1’s seal. Only an in-module semantic test type can implement it, and it still suffers the default/return-shape defects above.
   105	- “Sole entry surface” is currently false: ProjectResolver uses `WorkspaceRead` directly (`resolver.rs:321-365`), component-meta reaches the host/scheduler (`component_meta/mod.rs:251-288`), and dispatch lowering calls host materialization (`lower.rs:403-418`).
   106	
   107	Replace the operation trait with one closed, non-overridable inherent gateway:
   108	
   109	```rust
   110	pub enum NonFlowOperation { /* every C2-reachable operation */ }
   111	pub enum NonFlowValue { /* heterogeneous results */ }
   112	
   113	impl TypeInfoCore {
   114	    pub fn attempt(
   115	        &self,
   116	        observations: &ObservationSnapshot,
   117	        operation: NonFlowOperation,
   118	    ) -> AttemptOutcome<NonFlowValue>;
   119	}
   120	```
   121	
   122	Keep the implementation modules and fields private. Match `NonFlowOperation` exhaustively with no wildcard. Adding a variant then forces the dispatcher to change, while every cross-crate operation necessarily returns the one inherent method’s `AttemptOutcome`. Compile-fail fixtures prove foreign code cannot implement a query/observation trait or access an alternate kernel operation. This is a mechanically valid proof of the closed cross-crate entry surface and its return shape.
   123	
   124	It is not—and stable Rust cannot make it—a complete proof that every internal helper is I/O-free. `verter_semantic` can still compile `std::fs`, `std::net`, a blocking primitive, a global/TLS read, or an I/O-capable callback without naming `VerterHost` or scheduler. Cargo’s crate firewall cannot observe those effects. A dedicated `#![no_std]` capability crate could strengthen that proof, but the binding ruling requires the existing `verter_semantic` crate.
   125	
   126	The honest mechanically checkable criterion is therefore:
   127	
   128	- Every external C2 operation is a `NonFlowOperation` and enters through `TypeInfoCore::attempt`.
   129	- All kernel internals are private to that module tree.
   130	- The semantic Cargo closure contains only layers 1–3.
   131	- Compile-fail tests pin sealing and private-entry unreachability.
   132	- Exhaustive all-missing-observation tests cover every enum variant and require `NeedInputs` or `Terminal`, never blocking.
   133	- Internal absence of direct I/O/blocking remains an audited/linted source invariant, not a type-system proof.
   134	
   135	Accepted ADR: unchanged by all three gap resolutions.
   136	
   137	Program DAG edge: unchanged; the planned dependency inversion remains higher layers → `verter_semantic`.
   138	
   139	Program outcome: unchanged; full non-flow extraction and full behavioral `AttemptOutcome` coverage remain required.
   140	
   141	GAP 1 VERDICT — Current cross-crate sealing design is impossible; seal semantic-owned snapshots and require compiler/session composition, not foreign implementations.
   142	
   143	GAP 2 VERDICT — The proposed files do not close below layer 4 as-is; C1 is executable only through the listed splits, cuts, and capture inversions.
   144	
   145	GAP 3 VERDICT — The exhaustive-`impl` proof is false; a closed inherent gateway proves boundary shape, but total internal I/O-freedom has no mechanically valid proof under the preserved existing-crate architecture.

All four proposed positions fail. Forks 1 and 3 are one coupled decision.

First, the draft is factually wrong that both modules are private: `resolver_core` is `pub mod`; only `resolver_store` is private (`crates/verter_session/src/lib.rs:341-342`). That does not rescue in-place convergence.

### Fork 1 — VIOLATES

Invariant: inward, cycle-free dependency direction; compiler may depend on the semantic kernel, never on session (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/architecture.md:1110-1130`, `decisions/ADR-015-binding-dependency-direction.md:24-34`).

A `pub(crate)` session facade is unusable by C2. Making it public would require `verter_compiler -> verter_session`, while session already depends on compiler (`crates/verter_session/Cargo.toml:117`), creating a cycle. Compiler already depends on the ratified layer-3 kernel crate, `verter_semantic` (`crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:59`; `crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/workspace_dependency_layers.rs:44-47`).

“Prove extractability without extracting” is not mechanically enforceable inside this crate. The existing structural graph guard explicitly cannot see intra-crate direction (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/A5/dependency-direction.md:182-189`). A facade controls exposure, not what its implementation imports. The current context directly names scheduler state and `VerterHost` (`resolver_context.rs:183-196,700-717`).

Ruling: **EXTRACT-NOW into existing crate `verter_semantic`**, not a new `verter_typeinfo` crate. Exact boundary:

- `verter_semantic`: `ModuleResolverCore`, non-flow `TypeInfoCore`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, relation/node algorithms, dependency-neutral semantic store/value types, immutable observation contracts, and `AttemptOutcome`/`LoadSet`.
- `verter_workspace`/`verter_session`: observation capture, committed-store implementations, `VerterHost`, scheduler, I/O flights, cache-retention policy, and outer retry/commit orchestration.
- `verter_compiler`: C2’s concrete `CompileTypeInfo`, plans, facts, and anti-replay tokens.

The kernel closure must contain only layers 1–3 and exclude compiler/workspace/session/scheduler/provider. The existing Cargo-metadata closure guard is the landed structural enforcement (`workspace_dependency_layers.rs:1-18,316-350`).

### Fork 2 — VIOLATES

Invariant: environments provide immutable data observations, not resolution semantics or live I/O (`architecture.md:461,631,660-662`).

Moving that interface downward would preserve live workspace authority inside the kernel and let environments continue implementing resolution semantics.

This does not foreclose F1: F1 can later replace the capture producer with its coherent committed snapshot without changing semantic computation. Moving `WorkspaceRead` downward would foreclose that separation; its current methods are live authority calls, not captured observations. F1 requires one coherent captured state (`architecture.md:410-422`).

     1	# ADR-003 — Compile Semantics Use a Concrete Sealed Facade
     2	
     3	**Status:** Accepted
     4	
     5	## Context
     6	
     7	The compiler needs optional project-aware semantic projections. An open trait would permit alternate module/type/runtime-classification semantics and create a second engine.
     8	
     9	## Decision
    10	
    11	The compiler accepts only a concrete Verter-owned `CompileTypeInfo<'_>` facade. Lifecycle variants are private/sealed first-party constructions. External integrations may supply captured observations through a data-only environment; they cannot implement semantic behavior.
    12	
    13	All construction modes execute one profile-parameterized semantic kernel and one module resolver. The facade has no blanket `Send + Sync`; ownership/concurrency is a lifecycle policy.
    14	
    15	## Consequences
    16	
    17	Direct local, captured-project, in-memory, engine-snapshot, and validated-precomputed modes remain possible without opening semantics or coupling the compiler to `Engine`.
    18	
    19	## Rejected alternatives
    20	
    21	- public semantic trait object;
    22	- compiler receives host/Engine/provider state;
    23	- framework/compiler-local resolver fallback.
FILE docs/arch/refactor/rev11/decisions/ADR-011-staged-compile-attempt-and-input-loading.md
     1	# ADR-011 — Project-Aware Compile Uses a Resumable I/O-Free Transaction
     2	
     3	**Status:** Accepted  
     4	**Decision owner:** direct compiler/project TypeInfo integration  
     5	**Reopen only if:** a future compiler mode explicitly embeds I/O and accepts a separate architecture boundary.
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	
     9	A compile API that may need project inputs cannot safely hide I/O or retain OXC borrows across asynchronous loading. Projection facts must be proven to belong to the exact plan that consumes them.
    10	
    11	## Decision
    12	
    13	Project-aware compile follows:
    14	
    15	```text
    16	prepare -> plan -> project -> emit
    17	```
    18	
    19	- prepared syntax remains owned/borrowed by one retained owner;
    20	- the projection batch is compact, owned, and OXC-free;
    21	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized request to the prepared root; the plan contains narrower deterministic projection/product/terminal subplan tokens;
    22	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds to the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`, semantic profile, dependency/input basis, projection schema, and demand digest, so terminal-only sibling plans may reuse facts only when that projection token is exactly equal;
    23	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a first-class resumable outcome;
    24	- external loading occurs outside compiler/semantic compute;
    25	- no syntax borrow or unvalidated locator crosses the loading boundary;
    26	- each attempt reports the maximal sound missing observation set discovered;
    27	- retries use a monotonic progress ledger, bounded waves/resources, and deterministic no-progress failure;
    28	- stale or replayed facts are rejected before emission.
    29	
    30	## Consequences
    31	
    32	The same semantic kernel supports local, captured-project, in-memory, and managed-snapshot modes without hidden filesystem authority.
    33	
    34	## Rejected alternatives
    35	
    36	- **Synchronous hidden filesystem callbacks:** break hermeticity and coherent snapshots.
    37	- **Reparse/replan implicitly after every missing input:** can amplify work and consume mismatched facts.
FILE docs/arch/refactor/rev11/decisions/ADR-015-binding-dependency-direction.md
     1	# ADR-015 — Core Dependency Direction Is Inward and Cycle-Free
     2	
     3	**Status:** Accepted  
     4	**Decision owner:** crate/module ownership  
     5	**Reopen only if:** a new stable boundary cannot be represented without a cycle and an alternative decomposition has been disproven.
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	
     9	Where `CompileTypeInfo`, framework projection DTOs, and request contracts live can accidentally create compiler↔semantic or compiler↔session cycles, forcing traits, erasure, and shared ownership.
    10	
    11	## Decision
    12	
    13	Binding direction is:
    14	
    15	```text
    16	identity/span/language/contracts
    17	-> shared syntax frontends and dependency-neutral DTOs
    18	-> semantic kernel/module resolver/relation/flow
    19	-> compiler
    20	-> managed engine/session
    21	-> LSP/provider/MCP/NAPI/WASM/CLI adapters
    22	```
    23	
    24	Rules:
    25	
    26	- syntax/contracts do not depend on compiler, session, provider, or LSP;
    27	- semantic kernel does not depend on compiler, session, provider, or LSP;
    28	- compiler may depend on syntax, sealed semantic facade, and neutral closed DTOs;
    29	- managed engine depends on compiler/semantic, never the reverse;
    30	- provider lifecycle never enters direct compiler or semantic kernel;
    31	- adapters depend inward only;
    32	- durable build tests reject crate dependency cycles and forbidden edges.
    33	
    34	Logical owners do not automatically require crates; use modules/functions until a real dependency firewall or multi-consumer stable contract exists.
    35	
    36	## Consequences
    37	
    38	- direct compiler cannot become a session mode;
    39	- semantic kernel remains reusable across lifecycles;
    40	- fewer traits, erased bags, and `Arc` workarounds are required.
    41	
    42	## Rejected alternatives
    43	
    44	- **Mutual compiler/semantic callbacks:** creates cycles and alternate behavior.
    45	- **Everything in session/host crate:** preserves catch-all ownership.
FILE docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/compile-transaction.md
     1	# Staged Compile Transaction and Anti-Replay Contract
     2	
     3	**Status:** Normative direct/prepared/project-aware compiler protocol.
     4	
     5	# 1. Stages
     6	
     7	```text
     8	prepare(source, parse options)
     9	  -> PreparedCarrier
    10	plan(prepared, CompileRequest)
    11	  -> CompilePlan
    12	project(plan.projection_batch, CompileTypeInfo)
    13	  -> CompleteFacts | NeedInputs(LoadSet) | TerminalFailure
    14	emit(prepared, plan, complete facts)
    15	  -> CompileResult
    16	```
    17	
    18	Planning discovers the complete product prerequisite closure and closed semantic projection batch before projection. Emission does not discover new project-semantic demands. A new demand requires a new plan.
    19	
    20	# 2. Binding tokens
    21	
    22	`CompilePlanToken` binds the complete request for anti-replay. The plan additionally owns narrower deterministic tokens:
    23	
    24	```text
    25	ProjectionPlanToken   root + semantic profile + closed demand batch + kernel/projection domains
    26	ProductSubplanToken   root + framework/product + output profile + required product mapping contract
    27	TerminalSubplanToken  exact typed result/product + requested presentation/provenance/encoding profile
    28	```
    29	
    30	The whole `CompilePlanToken` binds at least:
    31	
    32	- prepared root/source/unit identities;
    33	- parse key/domain and relevant generation;
    34	- normalized canonical typed product-request collection;
    35	- shared semantic profile when observed;
    36	- each product's output and requested terminal presentation/mapping/provenance/serialization profiles;
    37	- framework/compiler compatibility identity;
    38	- projection schema/domain;
    39	- plan algorithm compatibility domain;
    40	- deterministic demand ordering and digest.
    41	
    42	The plan contains independently keyed subplans/artifact identities. A presentation-, map-encoding-, provenance-, or serialization-only change may create a new terminal subplan without invalidating an unchanged semantic projection or code-generation subplan. `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete request for anti-replay; it does not force every subartifact to use that whole token as its cache key.
    43	
    44	`CompileFactsBatch` binds:
    45	
    46	- exact `ProjectionPlanToken` and demand digest referenced by the containing plan;
    47	- semantic profile and kernel compatibility domain;
    48	- input basis and observed dependency fingerprints;
    49	- one typed result for every demand;
    50	- exactness/completeness/degradation;
    51	- integrity and size limits when decoded or transferred.
    52	
    53	Emission first validates the whole `CompilePlanToken`, then validates that the facts satisfy the exact `ProjectionPlanToken` referenced by that plan. It rejects missing, extra, duplicated, reordered without canonical identity, stale, wrong-profile, wrong-projection-plan, wrong-root, wrong-domain, or insufficient facts before output construction.
    54	
    55	# 3. Zero-demand behavior
    56	
    57	When the plan has no semantic projection demands:
    58	
    59	- no `CompileTypeInfo` session is constructed;
    60	- no module resolver or TypeInfo index/graph/flow work runs;
    61	- projection stage is represented as an empty complete batch bound to the plan;
    62	- Svelte current runtime compilation must prove zero Vue/native projection demand unless its capability contract changes.
    63	
    64	# 4. `NeedInputs`
    65	
    66	`NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a resumable orchestration outcome. It does not mutate the current plan or prepared value with unversioned ambient data. The outer orchestrator loads and publishes/rebuilds a coherent input view according to `input-loading.md`, then reruns projection with the same plan only when the plan’s source/request/profile basis remains valid. Otherwise it replans.
    67	
    68	# 5. Direct and managed modes
    69	
    70	- local direct mode may project from the retained root only;
    71	- direct project mode consumes an immutable caller-provided observation view and returns `NeedInputs` to the caller;
    72	- managed mode consumes one `EngineSnapshot`/`InputBasisId` per attempt and uses the outer commit/retry loop;
    73	- all modes execute one semantic kernel and the same closed framework projector;
    74	- lifecycle, retention, and orchestration differ; semantics do not.
    75	
    76	# 6. Error taxonomy
    77	
    78	Distinct failures include parse/preparation failure, unsupported product combination, unavailable semantic capability, `NeedInputs`, no progress, projection gap, unresolved dependency, stale plan/facts, profile/domain mismatch, size/integrity failure, cancellation, budget exhaustion, and internal failure.
    79	
    80	# 7. Required tests
    81	
    82	- plan once and emit multiple requested products without rediscovery;
    83	- simultaneous product combinations equal separately requested products where contracts declare composability;
    84	- different per-product output profiles coexist without a global-profile collision;
    85	- presentation/serialization-only changes reuse unchanged semantic and code subplans;
    86	- irrelevant product/profile fields are rejected or normalized away before identity construction;
    87	- zero-demand zero-initialization;
    88	- local and imported projection batches;
    89	- batched shared-root deduplication;
    90	- stale/wrong-whole-plan/wrong-projection-plan/wrong-profile/extra/missing facts rejected;
    91	- facts from a terminal-only sibling plan are accepted only when their `ProjectionPlanToken` is exactly equal;
    92	- `NeedInputs` waves and no-progress behavior;
    93	- basis change forces retry/replan as appropriate;
    94	- direct/prepared/managed output equality for equal product/profile/input contracts;
    95	- cancelled/superseded attempts do not terminally materialize output.
FILE docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/input-loading.md
     1	# Snapshot-Consistent Batched Input Loading Contract
     2	
     3	**Status:** Normative outer-orchestration contract.
     4	
     5	# 1. Kernel rule
     6	
     7	The compiler, resolver, TypeInfo, flow, and reusable query kernels consume one immutable observation view per attempt and perform no hidden filesystem/network/process/package-manager I/O.
     8	
     9	# 2. Outcome
    10	
    11	```rust
    12	enum AttemptOutcome<T> {
    13	    Complete(T),
    14	    NeedInputs(LoadSet),
    15	    Terminal(AttemptFailure),
    16	}
    17	```
    18	
    19	`LoadSet` is normalized, sorted, deduplicated, and includes the resolution basis needed to load/commit safely. The kernel discovers all independently reachable missing observations it can identify without fabricating semantic answers.
    20	
    21	# 3. Orchestration state
    22	
    23	```text
    24	attempt number
    25	current snapshot identity
    26	accumulated requested InputKeys
    27	accumulated stable positive/negative observations
    28	unique input count
    29	loaded byte count
    30	dependency depth/frontier
    31	basis-change/churn count
    32	```
    33	
    34	# 4. Algorithm
    35	
    36	1. Run the whole operation against snapshot `S`.
    37	2. On `Complete`, validate observed facts against `S` and return/admit according to the query contract.
    38	3. On `Terminal`, return typed failure and never admit complete state.
    39	4. On `NeedInputs(L)`, normalize `L` and calculate `delta = L.keys - accumulated_requested`.
    40	5. If `delta` is empty and neither the resolution basis nor any previously observed fact changed, return `InputResolutionNoProgress` with the unresolved set.
    41	6. Check configured limits before I/O: attempts, unique keys, bytes, dependency depth, and basis-change/churn count.
    42	7. Load `delta` through embedding-owned same-key I/O flights. Each result is `Present`, stable `Missing`, or transient `LoadFailure`, with typed metadata and basis. Public/external loader digests are hints: the committing authority verifies key/basis consistency and computes or verifies content/configuration fingerprints from captured data before publication.
    43	8. Conditionally publish all validated commit-eligible observations as one coherent input batch only if the project/configuration basis remains compatible.
    44	9. If conditional commit loses a race or the basis changed, capture the new coherent snapshot, increment churn budget, and restart. Do not splice data into the old attempt.
    45	10. If committed, capture the new snapshot and restart from step 1.
    46	
    47	# 5. Direct project mode
    48	
    49	A direct/project `CompileTypeInfo` over an immutable caller environment does not own commits or I/O. It returns `NeedInputs`; the caller may rebuild/extend the environment and retry. The same no-progress/resource rules apply to convenience orchestration APIs.
    50	
    51	# 6. Observation trust boundary
    52	
    53	- public environments/loaders cannot mint authoritative `ContentId`, `InputBasisId`, semantic read facts, or completeness evidence;
    54	- source bytes, declared language/source type, canonical source identity, package/config metadata, lengths, and supplied digests are consistency-checked at capture/commit;
    55	- the authoritative owner hashes/normalizes once per committed revision and reuses the typed IDs thereafter;
    56	- a sealed first-party `EngineSnapshot` may carry prevalidated IDs because the same authority minted them;
    57	- mismatched key/bytes/profile/basis is a typed integrity failure and is never cached as stable missing or complete.
    58	
    59	# 7. Negative facts
    60	
    61	A stable missing module/package/file may be observed and cached only with the complete resolution basis: parent/package boundaries, conditions, path/case/symlink/workspace policy, and relevant configuration. Transient permission/network/process/provider failure is not a stable negative semantic fact.
    62	
    63	# 8. Resource failures
    64	
    65	Distinct failures include:
    66	
    67	```text
    68	InputResolutionNoProgress
    69	InputResolutionAttemptLimit
    70	InputResolutionUniqueKeyLimit
    71	InputResolutionByteLimit
    72	InputResolutionDepthLimit
    73	InputResolutionChurnLimit
    74	InputLoadUnavailable
    75	InputCommitConflictExceeded
    76	```
    77	
    78	They carry unresolved keys and consumed budget without exposing sensitive ambient paths beyond the product's diagnostic policy.
    79	
    80	# 9. Tests
    81	
    82	- multiple missing siblings loaded in one batch;
    83	- transitive dependency waves;
    84	- stable missing negative fact;
    85	- dependency appears between attempts;
    86	- project/config changes during load;
    87	- repeated same `LoadSet` no progress;
    88	- loader partial/transient failure;
    89	- unique key/byte/depth/retry/churn limits;
    90	- external observation digest/key mismatch rejected before commit;
    91	- no semantic kernel I/O instrumentation;
    92	- final result equals an equivalent fully preloaded clean run.

   609	The exact Rust API may use separate types/builders. The invariants are binding:
   610	
   611	- `CompileProjectionBatch` is compact, owned, and OXC-free;
   612	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized per-product request to the retained prepared root for anti-replay;
   613	- the plan also contains narrower deterministic `ProjectionPlanToken`, product-subplan tokens, and terminal-subplan tokens, so a terminal-only change does not invalidate unchanged semantic/code artifacts;
   614	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds to the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`, semantic profile, dependency/input basis, and completeness—not to unrelated presentation or serialization fields;
   615	- stale, replayed, mismatched, or injected facts are rejected before emission;
   616	- no AST borrow, arena pointer, or unvalidated locator crosses external I/O;
   617	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a first-class resumable outcome, not a generic internal error;
   618	- the outer caller may extend a captured project view and retry under the load-wave/no-progress contract;
   619	- a project/configuration basis change invalidates/replans as specified by the token rather than silently reusing facts.
   620	
   621	One-shot convenience APIs may orchestrate local-only semantics synchronously. Project-capable convenience orchestration must remain explicit about loading and retry; compute itself stays I/O-free.

External integrations supply captured data observations, not resolution/type/classification semantics.
   632	
   633	No blanket `Send + Sync` applies. Parallel batches use staged prepare/plan, one TypeInfo owner with internal parallelism or explicit first-party per-worker sessions, and parallel emit when legal.
   634

   636	
   637	## 7.5 Closed framework projections
   638	
   639	The compiler discovers exact closed projection demands. Vue runtime macro projection contains only facts runtime generation consumes: prop/model identity, optional/required/default association, ordered broad runtime constructors, `skip_check`/typed degradation, provenance anchor, and exact dependency/profile basis.
   640	
   641	Projection follows imports, aliases, substitutions, unions/intersections, utility/mapped/indexed forms, `typeof`, enums, and supported forms only until the closed answer is known. Object internals are not expanded merely to conclude `Object`.
   642	
   643	Current Svelte runtime compilation requests no native compile projection unless a future capability ADR proves an official semantic need.
   644	
   645	# 8. TypeInfo semantic kernel and public API
   646	
   647	## 8.1 One implementation
   648	
   649	`TypeInfoCore` owns:
   650	
   651	- authored-node traversal;
   652	- binder/name/reference semantics;
   653	- substitution;
   654	- relation/inference;
   655	- effective typing;
   656	- recursion/work budgets;
   657	- query-specific projection;
   658	- exactness/completeness propagation.
   659	
   660	`ModuleResolverCore` owns TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution. Environments supply observations; they do not implement semantics.
   661	
   662	Direct local, direct project, in-memory, managed, compile projection, component metadata, effective type, and framework surface operations share these kernels. Lifecycle adapters differ only in data access, concurrency, and retention.
   663	
   664	## 8.2 No final general `TypeExpr`, with ordered cutover
   665	
   666	The final architecture contains no general recursive owned `TypeExpr` or `PortableTypeExpr` as a generic semantic transit IR, final cache value, compile projection contract, or public result.
   667	
   668	The cutover is deliberately ordered:
   669	
   670	1. freeze every current producer and consumer, including `IndexedReady`/lazy body lowering, flow content, component-meta native/compat, graph export, NAPI/WASM DTOs, and tests;

     1	# C3 — Project-aware Vue macro projection
     2	
     3	**Status:** PROPOSED amendment / LOCKED. **Predecessor:** C2.
     4	
     5	C3 retains sole ownership of project-aware imported Vue macro projection. It fulfils
     6	the closed typed project-information demands accepted in BV1 using the canonical
     7	project/type substrate. It cannot reinterpret framework options, replace Vue semantic
     8	analysis/codegen, invoke the official compiler, or introduce open-ended fact bags.
     9	
    10	## Closed BV1→C3 demand protocol
    11	
    12	Every demand carries the exact prepared-root `SourceIdentity`, macro
    13	`syntax_index`, closed macro role, closed product lane, typed subject identity,
    14	`TypeScriptSemanticProfileId`, and `ProjectionPlanToken`. A subject is the closed
    15	`TypedSubject { position, locator, lexical_owner }`, where `position` is
    16	exactly `TypeArgument`, `locator` is the content-free
    17	`MacroPayloadLocator` validated against the prepared-root identity, and
    18	`lexical_owner` is the exact `TopLevelOwnerId`. C3 lowers that locator through the
    19	canonical retained-snapshot service to owned `TypeExpr` typed IR; the demand never
    20	contains source text, an OXC/AST handle, a resolver callback, or a raw semantic query.
    21	
    22	The demand vocabulary has exactly one variant: `MacroPayload { role, subject, lane }`,
    23	where `role` is `Props`, `Emits`, `Model`, `Slots`, `Expose`, or `Options`. `Props`,
    24	`Emits`, and `Model` admit `RuntimeBindingNames`, `RuntimeConstructors`, `PublicApi`,
    25	`Tsc`, and `Declaration`; `Slots`, `Expose`, and `Options` admit only the three
    26	type-product lanes. When typed `defineProps` is wrapped by `withDefaults`, its demand
    27	still names only the inner props type argument. BV1 retains the wrapping syntax,
    28	association, and defaults application; none of them enters C3 demand identity.
    29	
    30	This is the typed-IR macro shape retained from `CLAUDE.md`: C3 resolves one typed
    31	subject through the single five-mode project dispatch and then applies a thin
    32	role-specific normalizer. There is no macro-specific resolver, eager unrelated-import
    33	walk, text reparse, or compiler-local fallback. Runtime-form object/array arguments,
    34	the `withDefaults` object and its eligibility/merge semantics, and all other
    35	source-local macro syntax remain parser/BV1-owned. They never lower to `TypeExpr`,
    36	enter a C3 demand, or get merged by C3.
    37	
    38	Each variant has one corresponding success payload:
    39	
    40	- `RuntimeBindingNames` returns `MacroRuntimeBindingProjection`;
    41	- `RuntimeConstructors` returns `MacroRuntimeProjection` with normalized
    42	  props/emits/model shapes and typed member degradation;
    43	- `PublicApi`, `Tsc`, and `Declaration` return `MacroTypeProductProjection` for the
    44	  named product.
    45	
    46	Every payload is wrapped in the closed result envelope
    47	`DemandResult<T> = Success { value, dependencies, profile, input_basis } |
    48	NotFound { reason } | Stale { reason } | Error { reason }`. `NotFoundReason` is
    49	exactly `MissingImport`, `MissingExport`, `MissingDeclaration`, or
    50	`UnavailableProjectInput`. `StaleReason` is exactly `RootRevisionMismatch`,
    51	`InputBasisMismatch`, `DependencyFingerprintMismatch`,
    52	`SemanticProfileMismatch`, or `ProjectionPlanMismatch`. `ErrorReason` is exactly
    53	`UnsupportedTypeShape`, `BudgetExceeded`, `Recursion`, `Cancelled`, or
    54	`InternalFailure`. Every arm repeats the demand identity; success additionally
    55	carries the sorted unique dependency identities and the exact semantic profile/input
    56	basis that produced it.
    57	
    58	Demand identity is the deterministic tuple of every common field above plus the
    59	`MacroPayload` discriminant. The batch order is source `syntax_index`, then role
    60	(`Props`, `Emits`, `Model`, `Slots`, `Expose`, `Options`), then lane
    61	(`RuntimeBindingNames`, `RuntimeConstructors`, `PublicApi`, `Tsc`, `Declaration`).
    62	Exact duplicate identities may share computation, but C3 returns one result per
    63	planned identity in that order. Missing, extra, duplicate, or reordered results, or
    64	any token/profile/root mismatch, reject the entire facts batch before codegen.
    65	
    66	BV1 converts an omitted result or any top-level `NotFound`, `Stale`, or `Error` arm
    67	to a typed `ProjectProjectionUnavailable` non-success at the authored macro/type
    68	anchor and publishes no artifact. A `Success` may carry only the explicitly typed
    69	member-level degradation allowed by its payload contract (for example an unresolved
    70	runtime constructor becomes `null` plus its typed diagnostic); it may never become an
    71	empty successful surface, silently omit a member, fabricate a reference, or fabricate
    72	a bound-free binder.
    73	
    74	## Required exit
    75	
    76	Exit proves every demand and result variant is exhaustively handled, source-local
    77	compilation requests no project data, and the real canonical project/type substrate
    78	obeys the identity, ordering, freshness, and typed-degradation rules above.

   111	pub enum VueMacroSemanticInput {

   115	    Tsc(std::sync::Arc<verter_macro_dto::MacroTscBundle>),
   116	    RuntimeAndTsc {

   130	            Self::Unavailable | Self::Tsc(_) => None,

   140	    }

   273	/// The producer's finalised fact observation set, carried across the scheduler
   274	/// worker boundary.
   275	///
   276	/// [`VerterHost::produce_vue_macro_codegen_with_ctx`] dispatches its build
   277	/// closure through [`verter_scheduler::scheduler::Scheduler::execute_scoped_cache_node`],
   278	/// which runs it on a scheduler CPU-pool worker. The fact tracer stack is
   279	/// thread-local with no cross-thread bridge, so the tracer the producer installs
   280	/// on that worker cannot reach the enclosing compute's tracer on the submitting
   281	/// thread — and a caller that joins an in-flight rendezvous runs no closure at
   282	/// all. This carrier holds the producer's observations plus its non-cacheable
   283	/// refusal so [`Self::replay`] can restate both on the CONSUMING thread; it is
   284	/// what roots the enclosing compile on every file the macro traversal actually
   285	/// read, including the transitively reached ones no direct import names.
   286	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   287	pub(crate) enum MacroFactFootprint {
   288	    /// A bounded observation set built only from publishable reads.
   289	    Rooted(Arc<[FactVersionRef]>),
   290	    /// A bounded observation set whose compute also consumed a read these facts
   291	    /// cannot validate. The facts still bubble into enclosing scopes; they must
   292	    /// never authorize shared-cache admission.
   293	    RootedNonCacheable(Arc<[FactVersionRef]>),
   294	    /// Finalisation exceeded the per-signature cap, so NO facts survived.
   295	    /// Replaying that as an empty observation set would root the consumer on
   296	    /// nothing — silently, and on exactly the wide-footprint inputs most likely
   297	    /// to reach it — so this arm can only refuse.
   298	    Overflowed,
   299	    /// The producer's aggregate basis moved while its tracer was open.
   300	    /// No fact set can validate that mixed world, so the consumer must
   301	    /// refuse even though the producer did run.
   302	    MutationUnstable,
   303	    /// No traced producer compute ran (cancelled, shut down, faulted, or
   304	    /// re-entrant), so nothing was observed and nothing may authorize rooting.
   305	    Unobserved,
   306	}
   307	
   308	impl MacroFactFootprint {
   309	    /// Split a producer tracer's finalised observation set into the transitive
   310	    /// canonical inventory the compile pipeline syncs as macro type dependencies
   311	    /// and the replayable footprint carrier.
   312	    pub(crate) fn from_finalise(finalise: FactReadSetFinalise) -> (Vec<String>, Self) {
   313	        let footprint = match finalise {
   314	            FactReadSetFinalise::Ok(facts) => Self::Rooted(facts),

    46	## Required exits
    47	
    48	`FC-VUE-001`, `FC-HYDRATION-001`, `FC-TS-001-LOCAL`, `FC-ATOMIC-001`,
    49	`FC-ZERO-WORK-001`, and applicable `FC-PERF-001` cells pass. Every BV1-owned or
    50	source-local Vue cell has no blocked official case or semantic known-divergence;
    51	jointly owned project-aware cells remain projection-required until
    52	`FC-TS-001-PROJECT`. Output parses, links to the exact packages, matches protected
    53	structure/topology, executes deterministically, maps accurately, and removes every
    54	corresponding BF3 guard. Vue RC maturity is not Stable.
    55

    57	
    58	Stop for a demanded project fact not expressible by the closed typed protocol, an
    59	unlocked compatibility change, an official topology the product model cannot express,

  1108	## 18.1 Binding dependency rules
  1109	
  1110	Logical dependency direction is inward:
  1111	
  1112	```text
  1113	identity/span/language/contracts
  1114	-> shared syntax frontends and dependency-neutral DTOs
  1115	-> semantic kernel / module resolver / relation / flow
  1116	-> compiler
  1117	-> managed engine/session
  1118	-> LSP/MCP/provider and NAPI/WASM/CLI adapters
  1119	```
  1120	
  1121	Rules:
  1122	
  1123	- syntax/contracts do not depend on compiler, session, provider, or LSP;
  1124	- semantic kernel does not depend on compiler, session, provider, or LSP;
  1125	- compiler may depend on syntax, the sealed semantic facade, and dependency-neutral closed DTOs;
  1126	- semantic projection DTOs live in a neutral owner and do not require compiler↔semantic cycles;
  1127	- managed engine depends on compiler/semantic, never the reverse;
  1128	- provider lifecycle never enters direct compiler or semantic kernel;
  1129	- adapters depend inward and do not expose internals back into core;
  1130	- durable build tests reject crate cycles and forbidden edges.
  1131	
  1132	## 18.2 Logical owners
  1133	
  1134	```text
  1135	Managed Engine
  1145	│   ├── SemanticGraphStore
  1146	│   └── ProjectSemanticDispatch
  1147	├── CssToolchain
  1148	├── ProviderHub
  1149	└── AuditSink
  1150	
  1151	Direct Compiler
  1152	├── shared frontend plus framework-native planner/codegen
  1153	├── request/owner-local allocators
  1154	├── fused one-shot
  1155	├── PreparedCarrier
  1156	├── sealed CompileTypeInfo
  1157	└── optional validated precomputed closed facts
  1158	
  1159	TypeInfo kernel
  1160	├── TypeInfoCore
  1161	├── ModuleResolverCore
  1162	├── relation/inference/effective typing
  1163	└── framework-owned closed projectors
  1164	
  1165	verter_tsc
  1166	├── Verter compiler/public projection
  1167	└── NativeTypeScriptCheckerClient
  1168	```
  1169	
  1170	These are logical roles, not mandatory structs/crates. Existing owners survive when they already satisfy the full invariant with correct dependency direction. A module/function is preferred until a real firewall or stable multi-consumer contract requires a crate.
  1171	
  1172	There is no generic publication coordinator, universal framework host, semantic scheduler DAG, general type IR, process-global direct compiler cache, or public alternate resolver.
  1173	
  1174	# 19. Public boundaries
  1175	
  1176	The direct API exposes a small typed vocabulary:
  1177	
  1178	- `Compiler`, `CompileRequest`, and typed compile attempt/outcome;
  1179	- `PreparedCarrier`, `CompilePlanToken`, `CompileProjectionBatch`, and `CompileFactsBatch`;
  1180	- concrete sealed `CompileTypeInfo` and first-party constructors;
  1181	- captured data-only project observations;
  1182	- dependencies, exactness, diagnostics, required maps, and retained weight.
  1183	
  1184	The managed API exposes `Engine`, `EngineSnapshot`, input/project operations, managed requests, provider configuration/capabilities, and bounded observability.
  1185	
  1186	Public TypeInfo operations use operation DTOs, exactness, dependencies, diagnostics, provenance, presentation when requested, deterministic stable IDs, and opaque session handles where continuation is needed. Graph export is separate and bounded.
  1187	
  1188	Public APIs do not expose OXC AST/allocator state, query keys, scheduler jobs, provider internals, mutable stores, raw semantic node IDs, `VerterHost`, or migration carriers.
  1189	
  1190	Every public type documents source ownership, lifetime, deterministic/stable versus ephemeral identity, exactness, failure, compatibility domain when one exists, and intentional `Send`/`Sync` behavior.

     1	# Verter Architecture — Revision 11
     2	
     3	**Status:** Durable normative architecture; implementation entry is governed by the Revision 11 readiness lock.  
     4	**Baseline-independent:** implementation evidence is recorded separately under `baseline/`.  
     5	**Breaking changes:** allowed and expected where they remove a harmful pre-1.0 contract.
     6	
     7	
     8	# 0. Implementation-entry lock and current-tree reconciliation
     9	
    10	The durable target is baseline-independent, but an implementation block is not. Before an affected cutover starts, the implementation checkout must record one exact SHA and reconcile every current authority, consumer, lifetime, cache, protocol, and test route touched by that block.
    11	
    12	Current owners are not presumed obsolete merely because Revision 11 uses neutral logical names. Existing registered-source/VFS publication, `resolver_core`, `IndexedReady`/`DeclBodyMemo`, retained parse workers, `ProjectTypeStore` cache families, `CodeTransform`, `StyleSyntaxIr`, component-meta native/compat paths, provider synchronization, and `VerterHost` responsibilities are candidates for **Preserve**, **Converge**, **Replace**, **Delete**, or **Defer**. Source evidence, not plan terminology, decides the disposition.
    13	
    14	No block may:
    15	
    16	- create a second owner while postponing the disposition of the current owner;
    17	- rename an existing correct authority and count the rename as architecture progress;
    18	- delete a current owner whose invariant has not moved completely;
    19	- implement against “an architecture-equivalent successor” without an exact refreshed baseline lock;
    20	- use this plan to override a current public/wire compatibility obligation that was not inventoried.
    21	
    22	The implementation-entry and reconciliation contracts live under `contracts/`. They are normative for block admission, not production runtime concepts. `program-dag.toml` is the machine-readable semantic sequencing authority; validated program state records execution, while PR stack topology is transport only. No block begins before all direct predecessors are accepted and the ledger marks it ready, except contingent upper-layer draft/review work bound to an exact lower predecessor in the same validated stack snapshot; acceptance still requires formally satisfied predecessors and restack/revalidation. Agent roles, context packets, worktrees, stack windows, review state, and campaign evidence must not leak into runtime APIs, artifact identities, production comments, or semantic behavior.
    23	
    24	# 1. Architecture constitution
    25	
    26	## 1.1 Product objective
    27	
    28	Verter is a deterministic, high-performance compiler and tooling platform for component frameworks. It provides a low-overhead direct compiler, an explicitly reusable prepared compiler, and a bounded managed incremental engine. These regimes share algorithms and semantic authorities but do not share mandatory ownership, synchronization, or retention policy.
    29	
    30	The architecture optimizes for:
    31	
    32	1. correctness and honest unsupported behavior;
    33	2. minimum work for the requested operation;
    34	3. deterministic output;
    35	4. direct compiler latency, CPU, allocation, copied bytes, and peak RSS;
  1000	- validation and admission;
  1001	- logical weight;
  1002	- soft/hard bound;
  1003	- eviction and pressure behavior;
  1004	- pin classes;
  1005	- follower behavior;
  1006	- shutdown behavior;
  1007	- metrics.
  1008	
  1009	Open current documents may receive protected capacity; superseded revisions are pinned only by live readers. Closed/removed files compete normally and become reclaimable. No cache relies on process restart.
  1010	
  1011	## 15.2 Persistence and precomputed facts are consumer-driven
  1012	
  1013	Persistence is optional acceleration and never correctness authority. Revision 11 does not require a persistent cache or public precomputed semantic mode merely because a value is serializable.
  1014	
  1015	Before implementation, a persistence ADR must name:
  1016	
  1017	- the current product consumer and workload;
  1018	- measured recomputation cost and expected reuse;
  1019	- complete semantic/profile/toolchain/source/dependency identity;
  1020	- compatibility domain and evolution policy;
  1021	- integrity/authenticity and bounded decode;
  1022	- corruption/mismatch behavior;
  1023	- retained/disk budget and eviction;
  1024	- privacy/security implications;
  1025	- clean recomputation equivalence;
  1026	- measured net win after keying, validation, serialization, I/O, and maintenance complexity.
  1027	
  1028	Eligible artifacts are deterministic, hermetic, independently interpretable, complete, and OXC/lifetime free. Never persist owner-local parse handles, AST pointers, snapshot-local handles, transient semantic cohorts, incomplete/cancelled/budget-dependent results, ambient-state-dependent values, or provider results without a separate proven protocol.
  1029	
  1030	Without a ratified consumer ADR, the implementation remains request/prepared/managed-memory only.
  1210	Production comments explain current invariants, safety/memory rationale, concurrency/ordering contracts, observable compatibility, or why a simpler-looking implementation is incorrect. Campaign history belongs in ADRs, changelogs, or git history.
  1211	
  1212	# 21. Anti-goals
  1213	
  1214	The following are prohibited:
  1215	
  1216	- conflating parse semantic identity with direct/prepared/managed ownership residence;
  1217	- requiring a direct compiler to consult or construct managed parse/cache state;
  1218	- building managed QueryRuntime/cache semantics on an unresolved or incoherent input snapshot authority;
  1219	- flight sharing based on an opaque policy ID, generic numeric budget ordering, or undocumented dominance; exact result-contract equality is default and any stronger-to-weaker relation is a closed proven query-family exception;
  1220	- silent semantic-profile omission of an unknown behavior-affecting option;
  1221	- public/precomputed semantic constructors without a current consumer and persistence ADR;
  1222	- cutting public `TypeExpr`/component-meta contracts before final flow/query foundations and complete consumer inventory;
  1223	- observable IDs or ordering derived from hash-map iteration, worker completion order, pointer address, or cache insertion order;
  1224	- a compiler-owned or externally implementable alternate type resolver;
  1225	- public `dyn CompileTypeInfo` semantics;
  1226	- a second flow CFG/control evaluator beside `FunctionFlowGraph`;
  1227	- derived graph indexes that become independent semantic authorities;
  1228	- one always-maximal flow lattice when a smaller product domain answers the operation;
  1229	- name-keyed flow state as authority;
  1230	- flow-private relation/disjointness semantics;

   564	# 7. Direct compiler, plans, and compile projections
   565	
   566	## 7.1 Direct compiler boundary
   567	
   568	The direct compiler is a separate product boundary, not an `Engine` mode. It exposes borrowed-source one-shot compilation, explicit prepared reuse, and staged batch planning/emission. It owns no workspace, committed input store, QueryRuntime, provider lifecycle, durable cache set, audit database, or background scheduler.
   569	
   570	No public `dyn CompileTypeInfo`, open resolver trait, `Engine`, `VerterHost`, provider state, or ambient filesystem handle enters the direct compiler.
   571	
   572	## 7.2 Typed operation plan
   573	
   574	The compiler consumes the final compositional request and derives the smallest acyclic prerequisite closure. A cold request plans once by default. Deliberate replanning is allowed only when benchmark evidence shows it is cheaper in total CPU, allocation, retained memory, and complexity than carrying the first plan.
   575	
   576	Unsupported product combinations fail before expensive work. No projection demands means zero TypeInfo construction/call and zero project read.
   577	
   578	## 7.3 Resumable projection protocol
   579	
   580	Project-aware compilation follows:
   581	
   582	```text
   583	prepare -> plan -> project -> emit
   584	```
   585	
   586	Conceptually:
   587	
   588	```rust
   589	let mut prepared = compiler.prepare(source_id, source, parse_options)?;
   590	let plan = prepared.plan(request)?;
   591	
   592	loop {
   593	    match type_info.project(plan.projection_batch())? {
   594	        ProjectionOutcome::Complete(facts) => {
   595	            plan.validate_facts(&facts)?;
   596	            break prepared.emit(plan, facts);
   597	        }
   598	        ProjectionOutcome::NeedInputs(load_set) => {
   599	            return CompileAttempt::NeedInputs {
   600	                prepared,
   601	                plan,
   602	                load_set,
   603	            };
   604	        }
   605	    }
   606	}
   607	```
   608	
   609	The exact Rust API may use separate types/builders. The invariants are binding:
   610	
   611	- `CompileProjectionBatch` is compact, owned, and OXC-free;
   612	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized per-product request to the retained prepared root for anti-replay;
   613	- the plan also contains narrower deterministic `ProjectionPlanToken`, product-subplan tokens, and terminal-subplan tokens, so a terminal-only change does not invalidate unchanged semantic/code artifacts;
   614	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds to the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`, semantic profile, dependency/input basis, and completeness—not to unrelated presentation or serialization fields;
   615	- stale, replayed, mismatched, or injected facts are rejected before emission;
   616	- no AST borrow, arena pointer, or unvalidated locator crosses external I/O;
   617	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a first-class resumable outcome, not a generic internal error;
   618	- the outer caller may extend a captured project view and retry under the load-wave/no-progress contract;
   619	- a project/configuration basis change invalidates/replans as specified by the token rather than silently reusing facts.
   620	
   621	One-shot convenience APIs may orchestrate local-only semantics synchronously. Project-capable convenience orchestration must remain explicit about loading and retry; compute itself stays I/O-free.
   622	
   623	## 7.4 Sealed `CompileTypeInfo`
   624	
   625	```rust
   626	pub struct CompileTypeInfo<'env> {
   627	    inner: CompileTypeInfoInner<'env>,
   628	}
   629	```
   630	
   631	All first-party local, captured-project, in-memory, engine-snapshot, and validated-precomputed modes execute one `TypeInfoCore`, one `ModuleResolverCore`, and one profile-parameterized relation/inference implementation. External integrations supply captured data observations, not resolution/type/classification semantics.
   632	
   633	No blanket `Send + Sync` applies. Parallel batches use staged prepare/plan, one TypeInfo owner with internal parallelism or explicit first-party per-worker sessions, and parallel emit when legal.
   634	
   635	Validated precomputed facts are optional and accepted only after domain/profile/toolchain/source/dependency/completeness/integrity/size and anti-replay validation. Callers cannot mint arbitrary resolved facts.
   636	
    50	
    51	## 3.1 Dependency direction
    52	
    53	Required compile-time or repository-graph checks prove:
    54	
    55	- contract/identity/profile crates/modules depend on no compiler, semantic, session, provider, or framework implementation;
    56	- framework compilers may depend on contract/syntax/framework-local code and the sealed semantic projection facade, not QueryRuntime/InputStore/ProviderHub;
    57	- semantic kernel may depend on syntax/index/contracts and dependency-neutral observations, not framework codegen or managed engine;
    58	- direct compiler has no dependency on `Engine`, InputStore, QueryRuntime, ProviderHub, durable stores, or LSP;
    59	- managed services depend inward on direct algorithms/contracts, never the reverse;
    60	- provider/LSP adapters do not become semantic authorities;
    61	- no dependency cycle is hidden through feature flags, build scripts, generated code, or protocol conversion crates.
    62	
    63	A machine-readable dependency snapshot is compared before/after every foundational block.
    64	
    65	## 3.2 Public and auto-trait contract
    66

   194	## Staged transaction and anti-replay contract
   195	
   196	C2 implements `contracts/compile-transaction.md` verbatim, not a paraphrase of it:
   197	
   198	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized request to the prepared root and everything listed at
   199	  `compile-transaction.md:30-40` (prepared root/source/unit identities, parse key/domain/generation,
   200	  normalized product-request collection, semantic profile when observed, per-product output/terminal
   201	  profiles, framework/compiler compatibility identity, projection schema/domain, plan algorithm
   202	  compatibility domain, deterministic demand ordering and digest).
   203	- The plan additionally owns narrower deterministic tokens — `ProjectionPlanToken` (root + semantic profile
   204	  + closed demand batch + kernel/projection domains), `ProductSubplanToken` (root + framework/product +
   205	  output profile + required product mapping contract), `TerminalSubplanToken` (exact typed result/product +
   206	  requested presentation/provenance/encoding profile) — so a presentation-only change can mint a new
   207	  terminal subplan without invalidating an unchanged semantic-projection or codegen subplan
   208	  (`compile-transaction.md:42`). C2 must not collapse these into one token "for simplicity" — that would
   209	  break the terminal-subplan reuse required by `contracts/compile-transaction.md §7`'s test list
   210	  ("presentation/serialization-only changes reuse unchanged semantic and code subplans").
   211	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds the exact `ProjectionPlanToken` and demand digest, semantic profile and kernel
   212	  compatibility domain, input basis and observed dependency fingerprints, one typed result per demand,
   213	  exactness/completeness/degradation, and integrity/size limits (`compile-transaction.md:44-51`). C2 defines
   214	  this envelope generically; **it does not define the demand/result vocabulary riding inside it** — that is
   215	  C3's locked `MacroPayload`/`DemandResult` (`C3.md:22-56`). C2's obligation is that the envelope's identity
   216	  fields (token, digest, basis, fingerprints) are validated independently of whatever payload type occupies
   217	  the per-demand result slot.
   218	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` from `project()` is resumable, never mutates the current plan/prepared value with
   219	  unversioned data, and the outer orchestrator (the caller of `project()` — today `host_compile_audit.rs`'s
   220	  transaction driver) loads/publishes/rebuilds a coherent input view per `input-loading.md`, then reruns
   221	  `project()` with the same plan only while the plan's basis remains valid; otherwise it replans
   222	  (`compile-transaction.md:64-67`).
   223	- Emission validates the whole `CompilePlanToken` first, then the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`
   224	  (`compile-transaction.md:53`) — two independent checks, not one combined comparison, because a
   225	  presentation-only replan can hold a fresh `CompilePlanToken` while legitimately reusing an unchanged
   226	  `ProjectionPlanToken`'s facts.
   227
